papers.summary: The water entry of solid bodies, in particular spheres, has been the subject of numerous studies due to its relevance in multiple applications, especially focusing on cavity dynamics and the resulting forces and subsequent trajectories. The role of wettability in cavity formation and sustainability has been experimentally and theoretically addressed in the past; however, typically only up to the occurrence of a primary air cavity pinch-off. What is less explored is how wettability can influence higher-order pinch-offs. In the following study, especially secondary pinch-offs are shown to determine whether a sphere trajectory is terminally ascending, i.e., the sphere returns to the surface, or terminally descending: wettability is shown to be a strong influencing factor. This study begins with a series of systematic experiments, comparing the entry and trajectory of spheres over a range of impact Reynolds and Froude numbers, but also with varying surface wettability. From time resolved trajectories, a force balance is computed, illustrating the role of buoyancy, arising from the volume of any sustained air cavity in the wake of the sphere. Secondary pinch-offs alter this volume; hence, the terminal trajectory. A force-scale comparison and local radial balance at the cavity neck are then presented, suggesting how wettability influences the secondary pinch-off.

papers.title: Cosmology with post-EoR 21 cm Intensity Mapping surveys: power spectrum measurements in the last decade
papers.summary: The technique of 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) is emerging as a possible, cost-effective method to supplement optical surveys to map the large-scale structure, and extend their redshift reach, with projects aiming to cover a large range of post-EoR redshifts, from z=0 to z=6. Since the early discussions 20 years ago, a few dedicated interferometers have been built, and surveys have been carried out using them as well as general purpose radio instruments. An introduction to late-time cosmology with 21 cm intensity mapping is given, highlighting the main scientific and technical challenges. We present then an overview of different instrument concepts and survey strategies, followed by a discussion of outstanding data analysis challenges, most notably the foreground subtraction, which is a major issue in IM. We carry on with a presentation of the currently active projects and the 21 cm signal measurements which have been obtained, either in cross-correlation with optical surveys, or as the autocorrelation power spectrum. Finally, we discuss briefly the prospects for this field with future instruments and surveys such as SKA, HIRAX and CHORD.
papers.comment: 32 pages, 3 figures, review submitted to Universe (MDPI)

papers.title: Observable-Specific Validity Tests for Scientific AI: Controlled Approximations and Intervention Response
papers.summary: An approximation can reproduce an energy while missing its response, or satisfy an error tolerance without being certified by a given bound. We formulate observable-specific validity records for scientific artificial intelligence (AI) that link a reduction to its reference model, error measure, tolerance, parameter domain, and transformations or interventions. Explicit displacement and velocity certificates for a singularly perturbed oscillator recover distinct convergence orders and provide sufficient validity guarantees. Exact Hubbard dimer relations resolve the different coupling domains accepted by energy and response criteria. Across 16 repeated neural fits, imposing dimensional homogeneity reduces energy scale transfer error from 52.3% to 0.0768% and raises the median fraction jointly satisfying gap and response tolerances from zero to 100%. Paired transformations verify the protected scaling relation, while a coupling crossover identifies the additional information needed for response transfer. A causal model recovers a positive intervention response beneath a strong negative observational association. For two mechanisms observed with Gaussian noise whose responses first differ at order $x^k$, we derive an exact fixed control query requirement scaling as $x^{-2k}$ and verify its full success curve numerically. Together with a 256-task evaluation interface, these results provide independently checkable tests of controlled approximation, physical transfer, and mechanism discrimination in scientific AI.

papers.title: Existence of the thermodynamic limit for the Hopfield model
papers.summary: We prove that the quenched pressure of the Hopfield model with $K\simαN$ i.i.d. symmetric Rademacher patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $α\in(0,\infty)$, finite inverse temperature and uniform external field, with no replica-symmetry, order-parameter concentration or non-condensation hypothesis required. The limit is the supremum over $r$ of limiting pressures of mixed models with $r$ binary patterns in a Gaussian bulk. Via the Hubbard--Stratonovich representation we extract the finitely many patterns whose hidden coordinates exceed $δ\sqrt N$; a collective interpolation replaces the other binary patterns by Gaussian ones with error $O(δ^2)$ uniform in the volume, and convex concentration on the discrete cube controls the disorder-dependent choice of retained patterns. For the mixed models we prove a Gaussian hidden-spin truncation bound uniform in the volume and in an arbitrary Ising potential, and convergence for Gaussian bulks with finitely many site-field types, reducing to results of Ho and of Chen, Ho and Issa on non-convex vector spin glasses with compact spins. For Gaussian patterns we give an alternative proof of the existence result announced by Camilli, Contucci and Mingione, extended to a uniform field and an extra binary pattern. In both cases the pressure has exponentially small deviation probabilities and converges a.s.; internal energy and entropy converge wherever the limit is differentiable. An extra binary Mattis pattern admits a scalar variational reduction. At zero field the Rademacher pressure dominates the Gaussian one with an extra binary pattern, which dominates the pure Gaussian one. No explicit formula is given. The proofs were generated through extensive interaction with the AI models Claude (Opus~5.5) and ChatGPT (Sol~6.1), based on the problem formulation and guidance of the authors.

papers.title: A Semiparametric Model Approach to Data Integration under Missing Not at Random
papers.summary: Integrating probability and non-probability samples requires accounting for an unknown selection mechanism that may depend on the outcome. We develop a semiparametric approach in which an unspecified function captures covariate dependence and a scalar tilting parameter governs outcome dependence. Identification follows from an instrumental-variable exclusion restriction and conditional completeness; a zero tilt gives a restricted missing-at-random submodel. We profile out the covariate component and construct cross-fitted, Neyman-orthogonal estimating equations for both the tilting parameter and the finite population mean. The resulting orthogonalized mass-imputation estimator supports centered root-N inference under nuisance product-rate conditions. Its linearization variance accounts for the probability sampling design and estimation of the tilting parameter. Simulations illustrate the cost of flexibility under correct parametric specification, protection against misspecification of the covariate component, and the consequences of invalid instruments or a misspecified tilt. A further simulation using 50,000 national health-screening records finds smaller bias but higher root mean squared error than a parametric competitor under the baseline instrument set. The proposed estimator varies less across alternative instrument sets, although weak instruments and smoothing choices affect precision and interval coverage.
papers.comment: 36 pages main text and 44 pages supplementary material. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23513896

papers.title: Adaptive Coverage Algorithms for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks in Dynamic Worlds
papers.summary: This paper extends an existing framework for the coordination of mobile agents in unknown worlds, by considering the possibility of dynamic instability. In the original problem, known as the Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Gallery Problem (POCGAGP) (arXiv:2512.09495), the multi-agent system must establish a communication network which completely covers an initially unknown constrained space. However, the POCGAGP fails to account for the unpredictability often seen in real-world deployment. To address this, the dynamic case (DPOCGAGP) introduces two settings which can influence the mobile network during deployment: Agent Loss and World Change, which represent dynamic changes to the world. Within this study, we present advancements to two state-of-the-art algorithms, the Centralized Agent-Directed Exploration for Network Coverage (CADENCE), and its decentralized analogue, DADENCE, to provide solutions in these cases. We then compare their performance against another state-of-the-art benchmark algorithm, and show that the adapted algorithms outperform across our benchmark test set, which comprises over 4500 test cases of varied size and structure.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 10 figures. Accepted to the 2026 IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference (URTC)

papers.title: Parametric inference for the average hazard approach in time-to-event analysis with sparse risk sets
papers.summary: The average hazard (AH) is a recently proposed model-free summary of an event-time distribution. Over a prespecified window $[0,τ]$, it equals the cumulative incidence probability at $τ$ divided by the restricted mean survival time at $τ$ and can be interpreted as a person-time incidence rate that does not depend on the censoring distribution. The difference and ratio of AHs from two groups, DAH and RAH, are between-group contrasts on absolute and relative scales without requiring proportional hazards. Existing nonparametric inference for AH and its contrasts is based on the Kaplan--Meier estimator of the survival function, and can become unreliable when risk sets become sparse or exhausted near $τ$, as may occur in stratified analyses. As a practical remedy, we investigate parametric AH inference using Weibull and generalized gamma models. We use maximum-likelihood estimators and corresponding confidence intervals for group-specific AHs, DAH and RAH in both unstratified and stratified analyses. Simulations show that under correct model specification, little bias and near-nominal coverage can be achieved in settings where nonparametric inference is inadequately supported by observed data. We illustrate the method using a randomized trial comparing neratinib plus capecitabine with lapatinib plus capecitabine in metastatic breast cancer. Parametric inference provides a practical complement to nonparametric AH analysis when sparse or exhausted risk sets make inference at clinically relevant truncation times less reliable.

papers.title: An exploration of in-band spectral index techniques for extended radio sources with EMU
papers.summary: Spectral indices are an effective way of differentiating between thermal and nonthermal sources of radio emission. Most often, spectral indices are determined using flux measurements taken over multiple observations with different instruments. Since these data are not always available, determining spectral indices from a single telescope observation is desirable. The reliability of these in-band spectral indices has not been well studied, particularly for extended sources. Here, we explore three different techniques for finding in-band spectral indices with the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU), a radio southern sky survey being conducted with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). These methods include: (1) integrating fluxes in sub-bands, (2) temperature-temperature (T-T) plots, and (3) using the ratio of the Taylor terms produced in the imaging process. We apply these techniques to a selection of extended sources of radio emission, primarily supernova remnants (SNRs) and HII regions, and assess if the indices produced through these methods agree with the expected values. For the SNRs, we also compare the in-band results to broadband spectral indices determined using flux values obtained from published works. We examine whether and when the in-band techniques can differentiate between thermal and nonthermal sources. In general, we find the T-T plot method to be the most reliable across the range of source sizes and brightnesses studied for both SNRs and HII regions. The sub-band and Taylor term methods can be useful under certain conditions but cannot be considered as broadly reliable for extended sources.

papers.title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
papers.summary: Identifying earth-abundant catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a central challenge in scalable green hydrogen production. We present a computational pipeline that couples diffusion-based generative modelling, machine-learning force-field relaxation, and graph neural network (GNN) property prediction to discover bimetallic HER catalysts beyond the structures and stoichiometries covered by existing adsorption databases. A generative model (MatterGen) is fine-tuned on bulk alloy structures labelled with their minimum hydrogen adsorption energy and steered towards adsorption energies near zero. From the generated pool we retain the stable structures that are novel bimetallic alloys: binary compositions built from the training-set metals but at stoichiometries or structures absent from that database. Each candidate's low-index facets are ranked by a machine-learning-force-field (MatterSim) surface-energy screen, and only the most stable terminations are converted into explicit slab models with hydrogen adsorbed at all high-symmetry surface sites and relaxed with the same force field. Two GNN surrogates (MEGNet and ALIGNN), trained on a high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) dataset, then screen the resulting slab candidates. Because the two models encode the local environment through different inductive biases, we retain only the alloys on which both agree, reducing the influence of any single model. This consensus screening, combined with a MatterSim energy-difference triangulation, resulted in a shortlist of near-thermoneutral bimetallic candidates. Eight are validated with plane-wave DFT, and four of them, Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3, bind hydrogen within the thermoneutral window. All eight alloys are dynamically stable by phonon calculations. These four alloys are highlighted as DFT-validated bimetallic HER candidates for experimental follow-up.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Transient Centers in Continuous-Time Systems
papers.summary: Analysis of mathematical models in ecology and epidemiology often emphasizes asymptotic dynamics, such as stable equilibria, periodic orbits, and attractors. However, many biologically relevant trajectories exhibit long transient dynamics in which a relevant observable evolves slowly for an extended period before a comparatively rapid transition occurs. On finite time scales relevant to data collection, management, and intervention, such transient behavior can be more informative than the eventual asymptotic outcome. In this work, we study long-lasting and slowly varying transient dynamics in continuous-time systems through the framework of nonequilibrium transient centers. These centers are points in the state space near which the observable can remain nearly constant for a long time, even when the full state is not near an equilibrium. We develop finite-time escape criteria for identifying such centers and their reachable counterparts. These criteria provide practical conditions under which nearby trajectories can remain in a slow regime for a long period of time before eventually leaving it. We apply the theory to an epidemic model with delay of stability loss. In this model, trajectories may remain close to the disease-free manifold for a long time before the infectious population resurges. The framework developed here describes this behavior as slow evolution near a nonequilibrium transient center followed by finite-time escape from the slow regime.

papers.title: Lifting the mixed to the pure: quantum phases of matter from canonical purification
papers.summary: Pure-state quantum phases are defined through finite-depth local unitary connections. This concept of phases has recently been generalized to mixed states in terms of locally reversible channels. In this work, we establish a fundamental relation between mixed-state phases and pure-state phases. We show that a locally reversible channel between mixed states can be lifted to a local isometry between their canonical purifications; thus, if two mixed states are in the same phase, then their canonical purifications are in the same pure-state phase. Furthermore, an explicit construction of the lifting isometry is given by ``half'' of the Petz recovery map, suggesting that the Petz recovery map \emph{without rotation} is enough to connect mixed state phases. We illustrate our results with two examples: toric code under bit flip noise and Chern insulator under fermion number noise.

papers.title: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision
papers.summary: With the surge of machine vision applications, image compression for both machine and human vision (ICMH) has become an important research area. Existing studies mainly focus on task-specific adaptation or multi-task joint optimization, yet they often overlook the unequal contributions of different features and network layers to downstream machine vision tasks. To address this issue, we first quantitatively investigate the impact of different feature and network layers on machine vision performance, providing a principled understanding of their importance. Based on this analysis, an Importance Guided feature and network Dual Adaptation (IGDA) framework is developed for ICMH. It adopts implicit neural representation as the basic architecture and designs an efficient adaptation structure with both feature and network weight adaptation. An Importance-Guided Network Adaptation (IGNA) module is developed with a low-rank adaptation strategy to selectively adjust key network layers according to their importance in different tasks. An Importance-Guided Feature Adaptation (IGFA) module is developed with a low-rank and Kronecker product-based transform to explore the non-local property of the features in order to reduce the number of adaptation parameters. Extensive experiments on representative machine vision tasks, including image classification and object detection, demonstrate that our IGDA-ICMH framework achieves significantly better performance than the existing implicit neural representation-based methods for ICMH.

papers.title: Current Sheets and Magnetic Reconnection statistics by Solar Orbiter at few to tens of Ion Inertial Lengths I: Energy Dissipation
papers.summary: In this work, we study the turbulent origin of ion-scale Current Sheets (CSs) and the dissipation of energy via magnetic reconnection. We analyze 103 hours of high-cadence (4 samples/s) in-situ ion data from Solar Orbiter, collected between July 2020 and September 2022. We apply an automatic detection algorithm that finds current sheets (CSs) of thickness (length in the normal direction, $λ$) near the ion inertial length ($δ_i$), and classifies them as Alfvénic or reconnecting. We compile a catalog of 974 CSs of thickness in the range of few to 90 ion inertial lengths, of which 53 contain an ion reconnection jet. We estimate that Solar Orbiter spends $\sim 1 \%$ of the dwell time inside a CS of few to 90 $δ_i$ thickness, and 0.06\% inside a reconnecting CS of the same thickness range. By comparing these results with previous studies we estimate that the abundance of CSs and of Reconnecting CSs evolves with heliocentric distance ($r$) as $r^{-0.9}$ and $r^{-1.5}$, respectively. We estimate that magnetic reconnection dissipates $ε_{rec}\sim 30 \hspace{5pt} \text{J} \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-1},$ in the $\sim 1 - 40$ $δ_i$ scale-range, by assessing the amount of plasma that interacts with a reconnection exhaust. We show how the dissipation of turbulence energy cascade by magnetic reconnection at scales smaller than 90 $δ_i$ is more effective closer to the Sun, and decays as $r^{-3.6}$. The current density of Alfvénic CSs thicker than the ion inertial length presents scale invariance, obeying $J_0/J_A=0.9(λ/2δ_i)^{-0.71}$, suggesting that CSs generated locally from solar wind turbulence.
papers.comment: Revised version resubmitted to ApJ; 23 pages, 5 figures. includes supplementary material at the end of the file

papers.title: Finite-Depth Null Capture and Mass-History Sensitivity in Vaidya Spacetime
papers.summary: We formulate a finite-depth endpoint map for past-directed null rays in dynamical black-hole spacetimes, retaining an unresolved label when no terminal is reached before a prescribed optical depth. For regular transverse terminal hits, common-flow, transversality, and separation hypotheses make the regular decision sets open and the endpoint label locally constant. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the resulting finite-depth capture circle converges to the standard critical circle as $\exp[-L/(3M)]$ when the cutoff is measured in static-observer optical depth. We then apply the construction to ingoing Vaidya spacetime. Two $C^4$ accretion profiles that coincide on a neighborhood of the observation event, and therefore have identical local mass and metric jets there, nevertheless produce distinct finite-depth critical angles. For the baseline protocol, $Δ_{\mathrm{hist}}α_{45}=0.0819062ε-0.0231767ε^2+O(ε^3)$. A backward adjoint gives an explicit causal kernel representing the first-order response to the mass history. The kernel is broad, peaks away from the photon-sphere dwell region, and changes between finite backgrounds even where their instantaneous masses agree. The quadratic coefficient is independently confirmed by centered nonlinear solutions and Richardson extrapolation. These results separate instability-controlled cutoff convergence from globally transported mass-history sensitivity.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables; ancillary code and numerical data included

papers.title: Stellar Kinematics and Molecular Gas toward NGC 6357: An Overlooked Earlier Stellar Generation
papers.summary: We investigate past star formation in NGC 6357 using Gaia DR3 astrometry and Three-mm Ultimate Mopra Milky Way Survey (ThrUMMS) $^{12}$CO($J=1$--0) data. A Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) search independently recovers the previously cataloged cluster G352.8+0.6 in addition to Pismis 24, G353.1+0.6, and G353.2+0.6. Isochrone fitting yields an age of $7.9^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Myr for G352.8+0.6, compared with approximately 1--3 Myr for the three young clusters. Assuming constant relative plane-of-sky motion, a linear traceback places G352.8+0.6 closest to their reference center approximately 1.8 Myr ago, comparable to their inferred ages. The $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ CO component overlaps G352.8+0.6 in projection and shows localized depressions in integrated intensity around three spectroscopically identified massive stars belonging to G352.8+0.6. The $-4$ and $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ components show complementary projected distributions and intermediate-velocity CO emission in position--velocity space. Assuming that the $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ component was physically associated with G352.8+0.6 and shared its transverse motion, our principal interpretation is that the two molecular structures interacted around the epoch indicated by the stellar traceback, approximately 1.8 Myr ago. The resulting gas compression may have contributed to the recent episode of clustered and high-mass star formation in NGC 6357 and to the formation of Shell A, which subsequent stellar feedback may have reshaped.

papers.title: Focusing through coupled multimode fibers for miniaturized single-atom tweezer arrays
papers.summary: Real-world deployment of quantum technologies requires systems in low SWaP-C packages. Quantum platforms based on ultracold atoms typically trap and control atoms with optical tweezers using light focused through bulky objective lenses, which are costly and sensitive to misalignment. Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer a compact route to focusing light, but their use in forming optical tweezers for cold atoms has been limited to a single fiber. Here we use a 2x1 MMF fused coupler to obtain two independent control paths sharing a common distal facet. We form near-diffraction-limited tweezers through each channel, suppress interference by applying a small frequency offset between the channels, and demonstrate that the tweezer separation is insensitive to misalignment of the input coupling. This work provides a route to reconfigurable single-atom arrays in low SWaP-C environments.

papers.title: Challenges in the verification of MOSAIX ASIC for ALICE ITS3
papers.summary: The MOSAIX is a wafer-scale, full-functionality prototype ASIC for the ALICE Inner Tracking System (ITS3) upgrade, implemented in $65\,\text{nm}$ stitching technology. It integrates 144 independently powered pixel matrices, eight $10\,\text{Gb/s}$ serializers, and on-chip data and power distribution, making full-chip verification highly resource-intensive (over $80\,\text{GB}$ of memory and 192,000 tests). Verification also targets a sophisticated power-up sequence and radiation conditions of $10^{6}$\ particles $s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and $4\,\text{kGy}$ TID. This work presents a UVM-based verification strategy that identified 260 design errors and summarizes key lessons from ASIC sign-off.
papers.comment: TWEPP2026, 5 pages excluding abstract and references

papers.title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
papers.summary: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $μ$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.

papers.title: Two-loop matter power spectrum from FFTLog and kite integrals
papers.summary: We present a fast and accurate method for computing the two-loop matter power spectrum in the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS). Using FFTLog, we decompose the linear power spectrum into complex power laws, reducing the two-loop corrections to cosmology-independent massless Feynman integrals of kite topology. A central numerical challenge is the evaluation of these integrals for complex powers with large imaginary parts, where the highly oscillatory integrands make accurate numerical evaluation particularly challenging. We overcome this difficulty using a Mellin--Barnes representation summed over a uniform lattice, achieving approximately ten digit precision even for large imaginary powers, with an error estimate for each integral. The resulting precomputed matrices allow the two-loop power spectrum to be evaluated for a new cosmology in a few milliseconds. Comparing with direct numerical integration, we find agreement at the $10^{-4}$ level relative to the power spectrum up to $k=0.2$ $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ after accounting for EFTofLSS counterterm contributions and FFTLog decomposition errors. The same framework extends to biased tracers and redshift-space distortions, providing the building blocks for general two-loop calculations in EFTofLSS. We make the code for evaluating the kite integrals publicly available, together with precomputed matrices and an implementation for the two-loop matter power spectrum as a concrete application. Our results can be directly incorporated into existing FFTLog-based codes for large-scale structure, extending their current one-loop capabilities to two loops within the same computational framework.

papers.title: B-ExposNet: Bayesian Deep Learning for EMF Exposure Mapping with Uncertainty Quantification
papers.summary: Electromagnetic field exposure in urban environments is highly variable, and conventional exposure maps provide a deterministic estimate, without considering its uncertainty. To address the gap, this paper proposes B-ExposNet, a Bayesian neural network for spatial exposure estimation with uncertainty quantification. B-ExposNet extends ExposNet by treating the weights of regression head as random variables, inferred by variational inference, so that the model provides probabilistic estimates from posterior predictive distribution. The method is evaluated on drive-test measurement campaigns conducted in three French cities, and compared with conventional method such as universal Kriging, in both predictive accuracy and the quality of the estimated uncertainty. On the test region, B-ExposNet achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 28.19\% and a continuous ranked probability score of 0.198~V/m, improving on canonical methods in both accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Safety Verification for Voltage Control in Inverter Dominated Radial Distribution Networks under Actuator and Sensor Adversarial Attacks
papers.summary: This paper develops a safety verification framework for inverter-based radial distribution networks under sensor and actuator attacks. Each customer is equipped with a droop-based controller to regulate its voltage within a desirable bound of a reference, i.e., to achieve safety. In our setting, attacks and disturbances enter the droop-based controllers, while actuator attacks corrupt the reactive power injected into the network. Consequently, invariance of the controller state alone does not guarantee compliance with inverter capacities or customer voltage limits. To address this challenge, we derive conditions to guarantee that the reactive power state remains inside a predefined ellipsoid, while at the same time ensuring that the attacked reactive power injections and customer voltages respect predetermined operating limits that hold uniformly for the entire predefined ellipsoid. Together, these conditions guarantee safety under all admissible disturbances and state-dependent sensor and actuator attacks. Finally, we express the resulting containment condition as a linear matrix inequality (LMI) feasibility problem. A five-customer radial network based on the CIGRE benchmark corroborates our theoretical developments in simulations.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Skill Retrieval and Arbitration for Optimization Modeling
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) can turn natural-language optimization tasks into solver-checked answers, but current agents remain brittle under narrative rewrites and often store reusable experience at the instance level. We introduce \textsc{ArchOR}, an archetype-centric skill agent that builds on \textsc{OptSkills} by adding two retrieval-focused modules. \emph{Centroid-Aware Representation Learning} (CARL) refines the ordering of cached skill representations through a low-rank prototype residual. \emph{Signature-Guided Retrieval} (S\textsuperscript{3}R) attaches open-dimensional structural signatures to skills, prioritizes candidates by weighted Jaccard overlap, and bounds semantic re-ranking to a top-$K$ set. A baseline-preserving arbitration rule determines when the structural route should replace the original selector. With the same DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone and released skill library, \textsc{ArchOR} reaches 65.00\% Micro-Avg.\ Pass@1 across five benchmarks, improving over \textsc{OptSkills} by 1.64~pp Micro-Avg.\ and 2.68~pp Macro-Avg.

papers.title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
papers.summary: An agent that must call several tools to fulfill a request fails when the tool retriever omits any one of them, yet tool retrievers are mostly built and evaluated on queries requiring a single tool. We compare representatives of six retrieval structures (flat lexical and dense retrieval, LLM query decomposition, LLM-navigated hierarchies, server-then-tool matching, dependency graphs, and trained set-level retrievers) across two multi-tool testbeds: 345 AppWorld queries with expert dependency labels and 103 MCP-Bench tasks over 257 MCP tools. We measure completeness@k, the share of queries whose entire required tool set appears in the top k, alongside the LLM calls, tokens, and latency that each structure incurs at retrieval time. A motivating analysis on all 7,961 ToolRet queries shows that aggregate completeness mixes two regimes: completeness at 10 is .58 to .67 on single-target queries and .08 to .17 on queries with four or more targets, and the ordering of retrievers on single-target queries reverses on multi-target ones. Across the two testbeds, none of the compared structures that is untrained on the testbed and makes at most one LLM call per query completes more than 10% of AppWorld queries at k = 16. The two structures that do better incur different costs: a set-level retriever trained on 75 to 90 in-domain queries reaches .33 on AppWorld and .58 on MCP-Bench with no LLM calls, while an LLM-navigated hierarchy reaches .30 and .40 with a median of 31 to 38 LLM calls and about five minutes per query. Their failure modes also differ: the trained retriever mostly ranks the missing tools just below the cutoff, whereas the hierarchy finds the target API and stops before collecting its prerequisites. In a downstream check with the official AppWorld agent, tasks with a complete retrieved set succeeded 21 of 21 times, whereas incomplete ones succeeded 2 of 39 times.

papers.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
papers.summary: Current LLM ensemble frameworks focus on multi-step setups with additional modules for answer ranking, often opting for token and span analysis rather than structured outputs, leading to heavyweight architectures with potential fail states along the pipeline. Faster, lighter solutions are more vulnerable to hallucination propagation and can lack output control in more complex pipelines. This paper proposes a customisable, lightweight ensemble workflow of coordinated Large Language Models that leverages JSON-structured outputs and anonymous peer-review ranking to mitigate hallucinatory outputs and single-model failure points. The pipeline is demonstrated on a relation extraction task applied to popular science articles in English, targeting four ontologically-grounded relation types (strong causation, weak causation, contrastive, and compositional), with semantic node canonicalisation and interactive, colour-coded HTML causal graphs as the final output. Performance is evaluated through an anonymous user study, achieving an average perceived accuracy of 0.778 against a human-annotated gold standard. The modular architecture supports flexible deployment across both API-based and in-house LLM setups, and the full framework is released under an open license to foster reproducibility and collaborative research.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, accepted at KG&LLM @ LREC 2026
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models Workshop (KG-LLM) @ LREC26, Palma, Mallorca, Spain, 2026, pp. 93-101

papers.title: Using Machine Learning to Measure Self-Efficacy Belief Through Learners' Interaction Traces in Technology-Enhanced Learning
papers.summary: Self-efficacy beliefs play a critical role in learners' performance, academic choices, and, more broadly, in their future career trajectories. As Technology-Enhanced Learning (TEL) environments have demonstrated strong potential for supporting both performance and motivation, investigating self-efficacy within such environments is of particular interest, especially for implementing remedial practices as early as possible to support learners' self-efficacy beliefs. Our research aims to develop a system capable of detecting low self-efficacy based on learners' interaction traces while they solve exercises in a TEL system. In this paper, we present initial results and future perspectives on a detection approach based on data mining and machine learning techniques to identify features indicative of low self-efficacy beliefs. Because the detection of learners' self-efficacy beliefs through their use of TEL systems remains largely unexplored, this work is exploratory in nature. To this end, we conducted an experiment across two universities to collect interaction traces and self-reported measures of self-efficacy. We then developed a machine learning pipeline comprising multiple classification models, enabling us to highlight the importance of closely monitoring of learners' self-efficacy beliefs for improved prediction performance, given their highly dynamic nature during learning.

papers.title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
papers.summary: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing them. Here we compare accuracies of chemical and general-purpose FMs on tasks from various areas of chemistry. Strikingly, general-purpose GPT-6 Astra outperforms the currently eligible chemical FMs on five physicochemical and quantum-chemical regression tasks when only 60 experimental datapoints are available. Only when provided 10x datapoints do the best chemical FMs reach performance of GPT-6 Astra: on 1,000 and 10,000 points they show performance on par with Astra on 60 and 1,000 points, respectively. Thus, counterintuitively, frontier general-purpose FMs are better suited for guiding chemical research in data-scarce areas than specialized chemical FMs, suggesting that learning relevant primitives (e.g. chemical structures) does not substitute training on relevant humankind knowledge.

papers.title: The Role of Electron-Nuclear Coupling on Chemical and Physical Processes
papers.summary: Over the last few decades, Born-Oppenheimer (BO) and Born-Oppenheimer-Huang (BOH) treatments for electron-nuclear equation of motion have been considered as the cornerstone for qualitative as well as quantitative exploration and understanding of chemical and physical processes. The BO approximation due to the large mass difference between electrons and nuclei as well as the energy separation among the electronic states could able to predict some of the processes (chemical and physical) satisfactorily at lower energy regime. Such approximation (BO) quite often fails for those cases with the involvement of excited electronic states, in particular, due to the coupling among the states. On the other hand, the BO treatment provides two important quantities, namely, the adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) and the nonadiabatic coupling terms (NACTs) determining the forces, which control the motion of the nuclei in a molecule. The NACTs play a major role in photoexcitation spectra, charge transfer chemical reactions, ferroelectric property and other processes, where significant anomalies are observed between single and multiple PES(s) results. Since the NACTs often exhibit singularity at the close vicinity of degenerate states forming conical intersections (CIs), such coupling terms could break the symmetry of the molecular processes changing the observables qualitatively.

papers.title: The 943 MHz radio-SFR relation of nearby galaxies observed with ASKAP
papers.summary: We investigate the integrated 943 MHz radio-infrared and radio-star-formation-rate (SFR) relations of 875 nearby galaxies within $D<50$ Mpc using public Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP) observations. After excluding galaxies with identified or candidate AGN activity, 594 galaxies remain in the AGN-cleaned sample. We used Bayesian errors-in-variables models that account for measurement uncertainties, intrinsic scatter, and correlated distance errors. The AGN-cleaned radio-infrared relation is nearly linear, $L_{ν,943}\propto L_{ν,\mathrm{W4}}^{1.09\pm0.02}$, with an orthogonal intrinsic scatter of $0.21\pm0.01$ dex, and is tighter than the AGN-host relation. For 592 AGN-cleaned galaxies, the radio-SFR relation is approximately linear, $L_{ν,943}\propto{\rm SFR}^{1.02\pm0.02}$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.25\pm0.01$ dex. Semi-calorimetric models reveal positive secondary dependences on stellar mass, $γ=0.09\pm0.03$, and rotation velocity, $δ=0.24\pm0.08$. The consistency between these two secondary trends suggests that the galaxy gravitational potential may weakly regulate CRE confinement and synchrotron-radiation efficiency. Our results provide an integrated 943 MHz radio-SFR calibration for nearby galaxies and show that, although radio luminosity scales nearly proportionally with SFR on average, weak secondary dependences on galaxy properties remain.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 9 Figures, and 1 Table, accepted for publication in APJ

papers.title: Calorimetry as inference: the information content of particle showers and the limits of energy measurement
papers.summary: A calorimeter does not measure the energy of a particle, it infers it from the record the absorption process leaves behind. Energy conservation writes every event as an accounting ledger, E = E_dis + E_B + E_esc + E_nu, of which only the dissipated component contributes to signal, so resolution is limited by how well the record of the dissipation constrains the missing entries. We formalize this: records form a lattice on which information is monotone; thinning a Poisson record scales Fisher information exactly by the retention; clustered records read out as sums cost the 1/(1+cv^2); and the quadrature budget a/sqrt(E) (+) b is the floor of every summed readout. The "ultimate limits" of hadronic calorimetry are identified as the first rung of a ladder, the residual spread of the invisible energy around a single correlated observable. We measure the ladder above that rung on Geant4 truth records of hadronic showers in copper, from the dissipated-energy sum to time-, position- and multiplicity-resolved records, with estimators validated on exactly solvable toy models. The achieved full-record value, model-conditional, is about 5.5%/sqrt(E) (+) 0.3% over 20-100 GeV, a factor 1.7-1.9 below the canonical one-functional construction on the same events (1.29% vs. 2.14% at 20 GeV). Under retrained high-precision neutron transport it moves from 1.29% to 1.30%, the dissipated-energy sum by 7%, and the gain from time structure becomes 0.17% in place of 0.28%. Dual-readout supplies the largest share of the information. Shower shape is next, almost entirely longitudinal, saturating at about one interaction length. Time structure adds nearly as much with or without shower shape, and stopped-muon neutrino losses set an estimated floor of 0.99% at 20 GeV. Every readout dimension has a measured information exchange rate, separating what new hardware can buy from what better algorithms can recover.

papers.title: Automated Keyword Generation Using LLMs in a High-Volume Data Virtualization Service
papers.summary: In modern data infrastructure, a data virtualization service (DVS) allows users to create many versions of source datasets for different processing tasks. For example, a multivariate or multi-modality dataset can be used for different machine learning tasks (e.g., classification, detection, segmentation, forecasting, and so on). Data selection, participation, integration, and preprocessing in different tasks result in many virtual datasets [Khan et al., SSC 2026]. Meanwhile, different users need to discover existing virtual datasets frequently and easily to avoid duplicate efforts. To enable an effective search engine in a DVS, it is desirable to automatically generate keywords for each virtual dataset. In this work, we present a solution for generating keywords for virtual datasets using large language models (LLMs). We propose five strategies for selecting different collections of text data for processing by the LLMs. We applied the five strategies to virtual datasets created in five application case studies with different source datasets. We conducted experiments with three LLM generators and two embedding techniques. The experiments show that the performances of the five strategies depend on the quality of the text descriptions. The results help us adopt a multi-strategy implementation of a new keyword generation service (KGS) as part of an extended DVS. The work demonstrates that the capability of automated keyword generation is indispensable for a high-volume DVS that is dataset-rich and frequently accessed.

papers.title: Online Learning of Heterogeneous Locomotion Dynamics under Reinforcement Learning Policies for Precise Loco-Manipulation
papers.summary: How to reuse a pretrained locomotion policy for precise loco-manipulation is still an open problem. We propose an online method to learn the closed-loop dynamics under a frozen locomotion policy. The learned model predicts floating-base motion and improves loco-manipulation accuracy. However, unobserved latent conditions of the policy introduce heterogeneous responses, meaning that the same observed state will lead to different motions. Direct learning without accounting for this heterogeneity introduces bias and fluctuations into dynamics estimates, degrading floating-base prediction and end-effector tracking. To address this problem, a contaminated Gaussian model is proposed to approximate the effects of latent conditions. The model uses two Gaussian components to approximate predictable and unpredictable responses under the same observed state. Then, the contaminated Gaussian model is combined with a Gaussian process to construct an online learner using random Fourier features (RFFs). The learner estimates each response's probability of belonging to the predictable component and uses it to weight online updates, capturing predictable responses while reducing bias and fluctuations caused by heterogeneous observations. With consistent and unbiased dynamics estimates, model predictive control (MPC) predicts floating-base motion accurately and enables precise loco-manipulation. A finite-sample error bound is established to ensure uniform convergence in online learning. Simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate consistent end-effector tracking across different manipulator configurations and tasks, with errors of 0.01 m.

papers.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
papers.summary: Scaling silicon spin qubits to fault-tolerant processors requires semiconductor foundry integration, yet it remains unclear how industrial fabrication and dense device integration affect qubit control and noise. Here we study ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ electron spin-1/2 qubits fabricated using Intel's industry-compatible 300 mm process and incorporating micromagnets for electrically driven spin resonance, using a high-performance device fabricated in the RIKEN research cleanroom as a reference. Primitive $π/2$-gate fidelities reach the 99.99% level in the Intel devices, which also exhibit longer idle coherence, weaker low-frequency correlations and reduced qubit-to-qubit variability across several measured characteristics. In the present Intel devices, the micromagnets are integrated inline with the back-end-of-line (BEOL) contact routing, with their separation from the quantum well set through the vertical stack design. Relative to the reference, their larger separation contributes to weaker longitudinal and transverse magnetic-field gradients. The weaker longitudinal gradient suppresses the conversion of charge noise into qubit-frequency fluctuations, whereas the weaker transverse gradient reduces electrically driven spin-resonance efficiency and makes drive-dependent errors relevant at lower Rabi frequencies. Additional BEOL routing and metal levels required for two-dimensional arrays make such placement decisions increasingly consequential when scaling. These results establish an integration-level control-noise trade-off linking micromagnet placement within densely routed layouts to achievable gate performance, while very high-fidelity operation remains possible in industrially fabricated devices.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 4 main figures and 5 extended data figures

papers.title: Reconstruct everything everywhere all at once: An end-to-end model for future colliders
papers.summary: We present the Reconstruct Everything Model (REM), an end-to-end multitask model for sparse, multimodal sensor data, demonstrated in high-energy physics. To our knowledge, REM is the first demonstration of a single learned framework simultaneously reconstructing multiple particle types directly from hit-level measurements across the silicon tracker, calorimeters, and muon system in a full simulation. It performs hit assignment, particle identification, kinematic regression, and resonance reconstruction without externally reconstructed tracks or calorimeter clusters as inputs. REM improves particle-reconstruction efficiency and purity and jet-energy resolution relative to both conventional and machine-learned particle-flow approaches. In diboson events, the learned resonance reconstruction improves W/Z mass separation relative to conventional jet reconstruction. These results demonstrate a reconstruction chain from detector hits to particles to resonances, with potential applications to structured prediction in other large-scale, sparse, multimodal sensor systems.

papers.title: On-Chain Behavioral Signatures for Classifying Centralized Exchange Addresses on Ethereum Using Proof-of-Reserves
papers.summary: Centralized exchanges (CEXs) are key gateways between traditional finance and digital asset markets, yet identifying their blockchain addresses remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on opaque attribution labels or treat exchanges as secondary classification targets, leaving generalization to unseen exchanges insufficiently examined. This study develops a classification framework using Proof-of-Reserves (PoR) disclosures, with 3,033,857 Ethereum addresses from 15 CEXs and five Non-CEX categories. We derive 58 on-chain behavioral features and evaluate LightGBM against logistic regression (LR) under a leave-one-exchange-out protocol. Across five lookback windows (30-730 days), LightGBM consistently outperformed LR, with macro PR-AUC increasing from 0.6611 to 0.9594 using the selected 17 features, compared with 0.7697 for LR at 730 days. Robustness checks showed comparable performance when feature selection and hyperparameter optimization were repeated across splits and held-out exchanges, while exchange-balanced reweighting improved macro PR-AUC. SHAP analysis and feature-group ablation identified gas behavior, ERC-20 token activity, and internal transactions as key predictive signals in the constructed dataset. These findings support interpretable CEX address screening for blockchain monitoring, while the released feature dataset enables reproducible follow-up research.
papers.comment: Accepted at the 7th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF '26)

papers.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
papers.summary: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. Through a case study in large-scale optical metasurfaces, we demonstrate DANO's full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and across drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design, with learned interactions validated through physics-based interrogation. As an AI-for-Science tool, it supports interaction discovery and scalable, customizable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, including virtual-reality optics.

papers.title: Unifying Data-Adaptive Longitudinal Treatment-Effect Subgroup Discovery and Pretreatment Membership Prediction
papers.summary: Precision medicine seeks to match patients with treatments from which they are most likely to benefit. A key step toward this goal is to learn treatment-effect heterogeneity from longitudinal study data. This requires discovering subgroups with distinct treatment-effect trajectories and predicting subgroup membership for new patients from pretreatment information. Existing methods do not fully unify these tasks. Covariate-informed membership models typically prespecify the subgroup number or covariance structure, whereas data-adaptive discovery methods often require prediction in a separate stage. We propose a data-adaptive semiparametric mixture-of-experts framework that unifies longitudinal treatment-effect subgroup discovery and pretreatment membership prediction. Subgroup-specific varying-coefficient functions characterize treatment-effect trajectories, while flexible covariance functions account for within-subject dependence. A covariate-dependent gating model links membership to pretreatment characteristics. A penalty on global component weights removes redundant subgroups, while separate gating coefficients allow patient-specific membership probabilities among retained subgroups. A blockwise generalized expectation--maximization algorithm estimates all model components under a single penalized observed-data objective. We establish consistent subgroup-number selection, convergence rates for the functional estimators, and asymptotic normality for the finite-dimensional parameters. Simulations show reliable subgroup-number selection and more accurate conditional membership prediction than a two-step procedure. Applications to the SANAD epilepsy study and the COMPETE migraine trial identify distinct temporal treatment-effect patterns.

papers.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents interact with external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), producing tool-call traces that may expose behavioral signals about users. In this work, we systematically study the risk of user-profile inference from MCP tool-call traces, where observers infer user attributes from protocol-valid tool interactions without access to user conversations. We introduce PrivacyTrace, a benchmark containing 1,000 synthetic user profiles and 4,000 agent trajectories across four domains, generated with real MCP tools from 25 servers. Experiments with four mainstream LLM attackers show that tool-call traces enable a 26.25% attack success rate for profile inference, compared with 17.97% from prior-based guessing. Further analysis reveals that tool arguments and returned results provide the main trace-grounded evidence, while linking traces across sessions further amplifies profiling risk. These findings demonstrate that MCP tool-call traces can act as effective behavioral side channels for user profiling, motivating the development of privacy-aware mechanisms for agent-tool interactions. Code and data are available at https://github.com/AI45Lab/PrivacyTrace.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 12 figures, 8 tables, including references and appendices

papers.title: Preference-Conditioned Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Terminally Constrained Multi-Objective Control
papers.summary: Multi-objective optimal control is commonly addressed by reinforcement learning with fixed scalarization weights, requiring a separate training run and constraint enforcement for each trade-off. This letter extends critic-free group-relative policy optimization to terminally constrained multi-objective control: a single preference-conditioned policy is trained over random preferences and returns a feasible approximation of the Pareto front in one run. Three structural results are established. Group normalization after scalarization preserves the prescribed preference, whereas per-objective normalization induces policy-dependent distortion; with pairwise distinct normalization scales, only single-objective preferences remain unchanged. A positive floor prevents the terminal-constraint multiplier from vanishing and renders the penalty exact when the floor exceeds a geometric multiplier. Deterministic terminal violation is bounded by expected stochastic violation plus a term depending on terminal-state curvature and action variance, so stochastic feasibility alone does not certify deterministic execution. On a heavy-duty range-extender powertrain with six stage costs and a terminal state-of-charge band, a representative training run places all 32 preference-grid solutions in band on six cycles inside and outside the training pool. Averaged over ten runs, the method yields more in-band solutions under deterministic execution than a critic-based conditioned baseline with the same terminal-constraint handling.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

papers.title: Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing
papers.summary: Knowledge tracing (KT) predicts a student's next response from their history. New platforms often have question texts but no response logs for training, motivating zero-shot cross-domain KT. Existing transfer and cold-start methods use question semantics, but cross-platform semantic discrepancies limit transferability. We propose TIZSKT, which separates behavioral sequence modeling from domain-local historical evidence construction and uses text as an index rather than a directly transferable predictive representation. The Mastery-Dynamics Encoder learns correctness dynamics without question identifiers or text embeddings. Domain-Local Question Addressing builds fixed question addresses using a frozen text encoder and an unsupervised per-domain projection. The Text-Addressing Kernel uses these addresses to aggregate the current student's previous outcomes into a question-specific historical correctness summary. Cross-Segment Continuation retains access to earlier responses without extending the behavioral encoder's input sequence. Evidence-Volume Read-Out preserves the total kernel mass discarded by normalization and combines its log-compressed value with the behavioral state and historical correctness summary to predict the next response. All trainable parameters are learned from source domains; target inference uses public question texts and the current student's observed history without target-domain training. Leave-one-domain-out experiments on three public datasets show that TIZSKT achieves the highest mean AUC and accuracy among evaluated baselines on all target domains. Ablations confirm the contributions of text addressing and cross-segment continuation.

papers.title: Evaluating Maternity Leave Reforms When RD Fails
papers.summary: This paper documents that expansions of UK maternity pay in the 2000s improved children's test scores while reducing maternal employment. Extending job protection alone generated similar employment effects but no detectable impact on children. None of these effects are recoverable with a conventional regression discontinuity (RD) design because eligibility is only imperfectly captured by the available data. We explain why existing corrections for measurement error in RD are not well suited and propose a simple imputation-based solution. The approach preserves RD's main advantages, nonparametric identification and transparency, and remains valid even when measurement error has economic content.

papers.title: The Unusual X-ray Spectrum of R Mon
papers.summary: The optically obscured young star R Mon illuminates Hubble's Variable Nebula and has historically been classified as an intermediate mass pre-main sequence Herbig Be star. We present Chandra observations of R Mon revealing a hard X-ray source viewed through high absorption from circumstellar gas known to be present from previous CO observations. The X-ray spectrum is characterized by line emission from the He-like Fe K complex (6.7 keV) tracing very hot plasma and fluorescent Fe emission (6.4 keV) from cold gas near the star that is irradiated by hard X-rays. Low-level variability on a timescale of less than one day is detected, but no large impulsive flares. The hot plasma and variability cannot be explained by shock models and magnetically confined plasma is inferred. The hard X-ray spectrum of R Mon does not resemble the soft spectra of prototypical Herbig stars but is remarkably similar to some class I protostars such as NGC 2071-IRS 1. As judged by its X-ray and infrared properties, we conclude that R Mon is a class I protostar and thus provides a rare snapshot of an emergent intermediate mass star enveloped in X-ray irradiated gas and dust.

papers.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
papers.summary: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution. Task-mixed flow-matching training jointly optimizes a single action expert across seven generation tasks, enabling direct motion generation from text, speech, music, and video. Multimodal Real-Time Chunking connects overlapping chunks under continuously updated instructions and robot states for continuous closed-loop execution. We further introduce Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video. Experiments show consistent gains across all four modalities when scaling execution-verified data from 1% to 100% and action-expert capacity from 64M to 911M parameters, while demonstrating that data quality and cross-modal supervision improve generation and execution.
papers.comment: Technical report. 86 pages, 31 figures, 15 tables. Project page: https://movens-zero.github.io

papers.title: Collisional excitation of HMgC$_3$N by He: rate coefficients and astrophysical implications
papers.summary: Reliable collisional data are essential for interpreting the rotational emission of HMgC$_3$N under the non-equilibrium conditions of molecular clouds. We investigate the rotational excitation and de-excitation of HMgC$_3$N induced by collisions with He, combining \textit{ab initio} calculations with quantum scattering theory. A two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) for HMgC$_3$N--He was constructed using the CCSD(T)-F12A method in conjunction with the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set. Quantum close-coupling (CC) calculation were then performed to obtain state-to-state integral cross sections and temperature-dependent rate coefficients for rotational transitions with $Δj=\pm1$, $\pm2$, and $\pm3$, covering rotational levels up to $j=20$ and temperatures from $3$ to $50$~K. The rate coefficients exhibit a clear propensity for $Δj=\pm2$ transitions. The resulting collisional data were incorporated into radiative transfer modelling to constrain the physical conditions and column density of HMgC$_3$N from its observed spectral line emission. A $χ^2$ minimization yields a best-fitting H$_2$ volume density of $n(\mathrm{H}_2)=1.233\times10^5~\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ and column density of $N(\mathrm{HMgC}_3\mathrm{N})=1.831\times10^{12}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. The derived column density is in approximate agreement with the observational estimate of $(3.0\pm0.6)\times10^{12}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. These results provide new collisional data for non-LTE studies of HMgC$_3$N and support a more realistic treatment of its rotational excitation and radiative transfer in molecular clouds.

papers.title: On the Geroch conjecture for toric gravitational instantons
papers.summary: Geroch conjectured that the local solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations with two commuting Killing fields and vanishing twist constants are generated from flat space by an infinite-dimensional group of transformations, and Hauser and Ernst proved this for stationary axisymmetric spacetimes near the axis. The solutions generated from flat space by the transformations with finitely many poles in the spectral parameter are the solitons of Belinski and Zakharov. We prove a solitonic form of the conjecture in Riemannian signature, for toric gravitational instantons. The proof combines Weinstein's uniqueness argument, a closed formula for the soliton metrics in Hankel determinants and a degree argument. It also applies to the toric Ricci-flat metrics with conical singularities constructed by Li and Sun.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum Algorithms for Trade Surveillance Analytics
papers.summary: Anti-money laundering (AML) and trade surveillance remain largely manual: rule-based monitoring raises alerts of which, by estimate, over 95% are false positives, each reviewed by a human analyst. We benchmark four quantum and hybrid classifiers against classical baselines on a synthetic pump-and-dump detection task: a fidelity-based quantum k-nearest-neighbours classifier (QKNN) with clustering-based routing; a quantum support vector machine (QSVM) on a one-body projected quantum kernel; a 20-qubit quantum neural network (QNN) with a Pauli-ZZ feature map and RealAmplitudes ansatz; and a hybrid quantum neural network (HQNN) in which a small classical network generates every rotation angle of a five-qubit circuit. Baselines are logistic regression, XGBoost, one- and three-hidden-layer neural networks, and classical k-nearest neighbours. All models share one stratified split of 1000 accounts (800 train, 200 test, 20% suspicious) and two 20-feature representations (ANOVA and PCA); QKNN and QSVM are also tested under simulated noise, and the HQNN is run on the ibm_fez processor. The best model is classical XGBoost on ANOVA features, at a suspicious-class F1 of 61.4%. The HQNN is the strongest quantum-hybrid model, at 54.5-57.9% F1 on an ideal simulator and 55.4-59.8% on ibm_fez, ahead of six of eight classical configurations; at a 15% false-positive rate, half its alerts are genuinely suspicious. Versus the QNN (42.0% F1), it raises under half the false alarms at similar recall with a quarter of the qubits. The QKNN reaches 43.5% F1 (44.4% under noise), above classical KNN (35.6%); the QSVM does not exceed 41%. We observe no quantum advantage, but a five-qubit hybrid on today's noisy hardware already matches well-tuned classical models, with room to grow via richer circuits and larger devices. We contribute a like-for-like comparison with classical models on shared data, splits and features.

papers.title: Safe Planning for Black-Box Systems via MAP Inference with Truncated Diffusion Priors and CBF-Informed Gibbs Likelihoods
papers.summary: This paper proposes a maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference framework with a truncated diffusion prior for safe planning (TDP-SafeMAP). Under a generalized Bayesian formulation, a criterion based on covariance condition number determines the reverse diffusion truncation timestep, and the clean control distribution predicted at that timestep is approximated by a Gaussian prior encoding the control regularities and uncertainty of expert data. An energy function containing a control barrier function (CBF) constraint violation measure defines a Gibbs task likelihood that incorporates physical constraint information. After fusing the prior and likelihood, the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), whose core update admits an interpretation as a sampling-based approximation to natural-gradient ascent, approximates the posterior mode using only black-box evaluations. Bézier-curve-based dimensionality reduction and related techniques further improve computational efficiency and task-completion capability. Theoretical analysis establishes an error bound for the approximate MAP solution, an explicit condition for CBF safety preservation, and the equivalence of the MAP problem under prior whitening. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently generates safe, smooth, and goal-reaching trajectories, providing an effective and practical statistical inference approach to safe planning for black-box systems.

papers.title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
papers.summary: We introduce a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence to evaluate one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation in the causal Loop Tree Dual (cLTD) representation. The key feature that makes this possible is the fact that for Euclidean kinematics all singularities of the cLTD integrand lie on a compact set in loop momentum space. We prove that our algorithm admits a stretched exponential convergence with the number of integrand evaluations, and we illustrate it by evaluating triangle, box and pentagon integrals at selected Euclidean kinematics points. We benchmark our implementation against analytic results as well as results obtained via Monte Carlo integration. We also provide a proof of concept that our algorithm can be extended to physical kinematics after subtraction of threshold singularities.

papers.title: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots
papers.summary: LLM-based robotic agent systems can generate programs for robot control, yet their generalization to new tasks often depends on elaborate scaffolding. Expanding their skill repertoires alone offers limited guidance on how to assess new capabilities or identify what remains beyond their reach. We introduce META-Robot, a framework that couples self cognition with capability scaling by expanding the criteria through which an agent evaluates and develops its skills. At its core, action-level predicates make execution outcomes explicit and available for LLM reasoning. The agent uses these assessments to identify its own limitations, extend relevant evaluation criteria, and guide the structured expansion of its skills. Proprioceptive feedback further grounds this process in the robot's physical state, enriching the evidence available for self-cognition. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate stronger overall task performance, generalization to new tasks, continued expansion of skills and evaluation criteria, and effective use of non-visual proprioceptive signals.

papers.title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
papers.summary: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

papers.title: Generative sampling with physics-informed kernels
papers.summary: We construct a generative network for Monte-Carlo sampling in lattice field theories and beyond, for which the layerwise propagation is computed and optimised independently on each layer. The architecture uses physics-informed renormalisation group flows that provide access to the layerwise propagation step from one layer to the next in terms of a simple first order partial differential equation for the respective renormalisation group kernel through a given layer. Thus, it transforms the generative task into that of solving once the set of independent and linear differential equations for the kernels of the transformation. As these equations are analytically known, the kernels can be refined iteratively. This allows us to structurally tackle out-of-domain problems generally encountered in generative models and opens the path to further optimisation. We illustrate the practical feasibility of the architecture within simulations in scalar field theories.
papers.comment: Proceedings of 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025), November 2-8 2025, TIFR, Mumbai, India

papers.title: Channel dichotomies
papers.summary: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

papers.title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks
papers.summary: Simulation benchmarks score robot policies by success rate, and every failed episode counts against the policy. Many of these failures are the simulator's fault, not the policy's; we find the cause and fix it. Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, we find that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way. We present SimuGuard, an auditing plugin for LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa and RoboDojo. It leaves the evaluation unchanged. At every physics step, it records the state and flags an object that starts moving at a contact faster than the robot's contact or gravity account for. It replays a recorded episode bit for bit, and it reruns the episode with one simulation parameter changed. With it we trace these episodes on RoboTwin to the collision detection of the physics engine: for geometry one to two centimeters apart, the engine reports a penetration of about two centimeters, and the solver throws the object out at several meters per second. The cause is one constant: the distance algorithm discards triangles below a fixed area threshold, which valid triangles fall below at the centimeter scale. With that constant changed and nothing else, episodes with an artifact fall from 12 in 100 to none, and the success rate on five container tasks rises from 89% to 98%. Success rates in simulation thus count failures that the simulator causes. Benchmarks on PhysX 5.3.1 or earlier should rerun in a repaired engine. Where the engine cannot change, they should report the success rate together with the range it spans when every flagged episode fails or passes: 75.8% to 98.5% around a reported 83.1% for LingBot-VA.

papers.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
papers.summary: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. While faithful to the underlying XAI methods, these pipelines are hard to adapt and often struggle with context-dependent follow-up questions. We present SimXAI, a lightweight LLM-centric conversational layer that replaces these modules with a single tool-calling LLM that bridges access to existing XAI resources. Rather than a standalone agent, SimXAI serves as a modular interface that enables conversational access to external XAI resources.
