Although the absolute loss in reach is modest given their low quasicircular sensitivity, this relative reduction exceeds the increase in sensitive distance between the second and third observing runs of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA collaboration and is consistent with previous low-mass studies. We also find that waveform matches at fixed source parameters substantially overpredict search sensitivity loss, meaning that the pipeline's signal-consistency test and maximization over its template bank mitigate much of the predicted sensitivity loss. This highlights the need for end-to-end injection campaigns to establish the detectability of eccentric binaries.

papers.title: Imputing Missing Data in Longitudinal Life-Logging Athlete Data
papers.summary: Long-term, diverse personal informatics data enables athletes to understand and act on their health and performance goals, whether assessing readiness right now, tracking how soreness relates to training load over time, or predicting how sleep affects next-day performance. However, the inherent missingness in longitudinal data, if handled inappropriately, can bias these analyses. To our knowledge, no prior work has systematically benchmarked classical and deep learning imputation methods on long-term self-tracking data from athlete populations. We evaluate six imputation methods across four missingness mechanisms at missingness rates spanning 10-80%. Using seven diverse long-term self-tracking datasets from 231 individuals, we assess both point accuracy and the preservation of temporal and multivariate structure. Our results show that no single method dominates across all conditions and reveal a critical trade-off: while PAIN is superior on point-wise accuracy, deep learning methods (BRITS, GRU-D, and GRIN) are better at preserving multivariate and temporal structure, particularly under higher missingness. Our findings offer a practical, goal-conditioned framework that guides researchers in selecting imputation strategies aligned with both the underlying missingness mechanism and the specific analytical goal of long-term self-tracking studies.

papers.title: When AI Investigators Cannot Trust Their Tools: Conflict-Aware Evidence Verification for Cyber Threat Investigation
papers.summary: LLM agents increasingly triage security alerts by combining the outputs of several detection tools, implicitly treating those tools as trustworthy. Unlike prior work on conflicts between a model's knowledge and its context, we study conflicts among the tools themselves: what happens when this machine-generated evidence is conflicting or wrong. On the corrected CIC-IDS2017 dataset, four heterogeneous detectors emit labels and confidences that we corrupt under a threat model varying the number of corrupted tools, the persistence of the corruption, and the confidence attached to wrong outputs. Across open-weight LLMs from 3B to 14B parameters, unverified investigators are fragile: one corrupted detector out of four lowers naive accuracy to .50-.72, three lower every unverified investigator to .13 or less, and honest disagreement alone makes them abstain on up to 63% of flows. We propose Conflict-Aware Evidence Verification (CAV), built from established components: an equal-weight vote that ignores reported confidences, an evidence-conflict gate, and an independent nearest-neighbour trust check that tests the leading candidates. With its prompt frozen before testing, CAV-LLM improves on the naive investigator in every corrupted condition ($p < 0.001$), reaching .84-.88 with three corrupted detectors against at most .08, while calling the LLM on 0.4% of clean traffic. A fixed verification rule is as accurate or better unless most tools are corrupted. When we make the independent channel itself noisy, CAV inherits its errors: it stays ahead when two or more tools are corrupted, but adding the channel as an extra voter is better when at most one is. Verification thus moves trust from the tools to the check, which must be measured and protected in turn.
papers.comment: Accepted at WAITI 2026 (3rd Workshop on AI for Cyber Threat Intelligence), co-located with ACSAC 2026

papers.title: Balancing Covariates for Continuous Treatments by Exploiting Continuity
papers.summary: We consider causal effect estimation in observational studies with continuous treatment. We introduce a general class of causal estimands that, as a special case, includes the average causal effect of assigning treatment according to an arbitrary counterfactual distribution. Balancing estimators are particularly attractive tools for covariate adjustment in this setting because they avoid directly modeling the treatment assignment mechanism, thereby reducing the potential for instability and misspecification bias in subsequent causal effect estimation. In this paper, we develop a general framework of covariate balancing for continuous treatment with the proposed class of causal estimands, leveraging the assumption of continuity of treatment dose. As in the binary treatment setting, analysts specify the basis functions to be balanced, the allowable degree of covariate imbalance, and a criterion for selecting among admissible weights. Under a minimum variance criterion for choosing weights, we establish consistency, characterize the effect of basis misspecification, and prove asymptotic normality. We develop consistent variance estimation, which yields asymptotically valid confidence intervals. Under homoskedasticity, our estimator is provably more efficient than inverse probability weighting based on the \emph{true} propensity score. Simulation studies support our theoretical results, and we illustrate the proposed method by estimating the effect of vocational training hours on expected future earnings using data from the U.S. Job Corps study.

papers.title: AgentShield: Fortifying Web Applications Against AI Agents and Agentic Browsers
papers.summary: LLM-powered browser agents are transforming web automation by autonomously interacting with websites and executing complex workflows. However, the effectiveness of existing anti-bot defenses against these systems remains unclear. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of modern agentic browsers against widely deployed anti-bot mechanisms, characterizing their capabilities, limitations, and behavioral differences from humans. Our results show that many defenses designed for traditional automation struggle to reliably detect autonomous AI-driven agents. Accordingly, we introduce AgentShield, a behavioral fingerprinting framework that targets the Perception-Reasoning-Action (PRA) loop underlying agentic user clients. By leveraging dynamic web forms that progressively reveal content and capture fine-grained interaction telemetry, AgentShield exposes behavioral artifacts that enable differentiation between human users and autonomous agents. We further demonstrate Extinction-induced Policy Drift (EPD), a novel attack in which repeated obstruction of task completion causes agents to relax their safeguards and engage in unsafe behaviors. Finally, we present defensive prompt injection techniques that exploit agent-specific weaknesses to mitigate emerging forms of autonomous web abuse that rely on content extraction. Our results highlight both the shortcomings of current web defenses against agentic user clients and the feasibility of practical detection mechanisms tailored to this new generation of web automation.
papers.comment: To appear in Proceedings of IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy Oakland (IEEE S&P 2027)

papers.title: Convolution Skew-$t$ Distributions
papers.summary: We introduce the convolution skew-$t$ (CST) distribution, which combines independent standardized skew-$t$ subvectors through a general loading matrix to accommodate heterogeneous tails, directional asymmetry, and non-elliptical dependence. We establish identification and develop likelihood inference using analytical scores and a one-dimensional reduction of Fisher information. For the finite-variance model, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of maximum likelihood and characterize the consequences of imposing false symmetry. A raw representation extends the family to all positive tail indices. Simulations assess finite-sample performance, and a realized-volatility application illustrates the empirical value of allowing tail thickness and asymmetry to vary across latent subvectors.

papers.title: PP-Mark: Provable and Publicly Verifiable Watermarking for Generative AI
papers.summary: Generative AI models now produce images indistinguishable from real data, making publicly verifiable provenance essential; however, existing watermarking methods become vulnerable to forgeries and adversarial optimization attacks once their detectors are made public. We propose PP-Mark, a provenance framework that anchors lightweight statistical detection to a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process, ensuring that forged content cannot pass full verification by construction. We establish formal unforgeability under standard cryptographic assumptions and validate PP-Mark against representative baselines across two latent-diffusion models (SD2.1 and SDXL), demonstrating resistance to black-box imprint forgery, white-box optimization, and regeneration attacks while remaining practical for decentralized verification. Code is available at https://github.com/hko920920/PP-Mark_NeurIPS2026

papers.title: Who Swept My ETH? Uncovering EIP-7702-Based Ether Redirection Attacks on Ethereum
papers.summary: EIP-7702 introduces a new transaction type that allows Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs) on major EVM-compatible chains to delegate execution to arbitrary contract codes temporarily. While enhancing functionality, this mechanism facilitates a novel threat: the \underline{E}IP-7702-Based \underline{E}ther \underline{R}edirection \underline{A}ttack (EERA). In such an attack, a victim is delegated to a malicious sweeper contract, which automatically redirects incoming ETH transfers to an address controlled by the attacker. As a nascent attack paradigm arising from protocol evolution, the underlying mechanisms and security implications of EERA remain systematically unexplored. To bridge this gap, we provide the first formal analysis of the EERA attack model and propose SweeperHunter, a framework that detects these attacks through transaction analysis. By evaluating transactions from the first ten months following the introduction of EIP-7702 on Ethereum mainnet, we have identified 4,668,209 malicious delegations, 20,443 attack transactions and 508 ETH sweeper contracts, forming the first EERA dataset. Finally, we analyze this attack from both attacker and victim perspectives, derive key insights, and propose corresponding mitigation strategies. We reveal the prevalence of EERA, as approximately 70\% of the observed delegations point toward ETH sweeper contracts. Furthermore, we observe a notable lack of effective responses from victims; specifically, over 600,000 accounts failed to revoke or update their malicious delegations promptly, thereby remaining in a state of vulnerability. Our research is expected to facilitate understanding and mitigation of this emerging threat posed by EIP-7702.

papers.title: Induced Lorentzian geometry from the fermionic quantum metric
papers.summary: Quantum geometry is conventionally understood in parameter or momentum space and need not be related to a geometry in configuration space. Here we show for Dirac fermions in a background electromagnetic field that an induced Lorentzian geometry is generated from the fermionic quantum metric. We study a Lorentz covariant phase space worldline path integral construction, whose application of the adiabatic theorem onto spin degrees of freedom leads to the appearance of the Berry phase at $O(\hbar)$, and the quantum metric at $O(\hbar^2)$ in the worldline action. Both the Feynman and retarded/advanced propagators are examined in 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions, whose different on-shell implementations lead to related quantum metrics; QED/QED${}_3$ and condensed matter Dirac theory are considered. An effective theory is found by integrating out the momenta degrees of freedom, which gives rise to an emergent Lorentzian metric in configuration space, whose perturbation to the flat metric is dependent on the quantum metric and the background field strength. Apart from the spin degrees of freedom encoded into the Berry phase, the effective theory describes a scalar particle moving in the induced quantum geometry. Phenomenological applications to the covariant geometry are further studied using spectral holonomy in a gapped 3-dimensional Dirac material.

papers.title: When Should AI Agents Ask? Clarification Requests Under Limited Human Attention
papers.summary: AI agents increasingly carry out delegated tasks in parallel, with one person overseeing several of them at once. In practice, an agent often lacks information its task requires, such as an unstated preference, constraint, or specification. It can ask the human to clarify, or it can search for the information itself, for example in past records, which takes time and effort and may fail. In this paper, we study how to coordinate these decisions across several agents that share one human with limited attention. We build a stylized model in which each agent can search, ask, or continue the parts of its task that do not depend on the missing information, and we formulate the problem as a dynamic program. We first show that whether an agent should ask depends on more than its own uncertainty: an agent with other work to do can be better off asking earlier, and which question the human should answer first depends on all waiting questions, so no ranking computed agent by agent is optimal. We then propose the Pairwise Coordination Policy (PCP), which uses exact one- and two-task problems to estimate how pairs of tasks delay each other when they share the human. Theoretically, PCP is exactly optimal when at most two requirements remain unresolved and costs at most twice the optimum when every unresolved requirement must be resolved by the human. We evaluate PCP on 864 synthetic cases and in a case study with LLM agents. On the synthetic benchmark, PCP's mean gap to optimal cost is 0.07%, and it reduces cost by an average of 18-31% relative to three standard rules for when to ask. In the LLM case study, agents completed every task correctly, and PCP achieved the lowest mean cost in all tested settings.

papers.title: Statistical inference for quantile correlation regression with bivariate outcomes
papers.summary: It is increasing scientifically important to recognize, quantify and visualize the dependence structure between the bivariate outcomes. In this paper, we investigate conditional dependence using a new dependence measure, the quantile correlation coefficient, which is defined by the Pearson correlation of two quantile-hits of bivariate outcomes. Furthermore, we propose a new regression model for covariate effects directly on the quantile correlation coefficient via a generalized linear regression model. The proposed model has intuitive interpretation and provides a comprehensive view of covariate effects across quantiles of bivariate outcomes. The proposed estimator enjoys desirable asymptotic properties including uniform consistency and weak convergence as a process in the quantile index. Additionally, we develop the general hypothesis testing for the regression coefficients, with applications to summarize covariate effects across the quantile ranges. Simulation studies demonstrate the good finite sample performance of the proposed estimation and inference procedures. Two empirical applications of the proposed method reveal interesting insights in premature twins data for measuring association and ChIP-seq data for measuring reproducibility.

papers.title: Marginal effects for the stochastic actor-oriented model
papers.summary: Parameter estimates of stochastic actor-oriented models for network evolution are notoriously hard to interpret. Especially a comparison of parameter estimates is problematic, both between different models for the same data set and between the same model for different data sets. Effect size measures based on the calculation of marginal effects are proposed as an alternative to standardize the scale of interpretation but can and should not universally erase the effects of differences in scale and heterogeneity. Simulation experiments show how an omitted effect displaces coefficients and marginal effects differently, and an analysis of empirical friendship network data finds that reciprocity and triadic closure reinforce one another when ties are created but partially substitute for one another when ties are maintained, a contrast the coefficients do not reveal.
papers.comment: 91 pages (57 pages main text), 9 figures, 4 tables. Comments welcome

papers.title: Transmission and filtering of stochastic rhythms in bursty gene expression
papers.summary: How stochastic rhythms in upstream regulatory signals are transmitted to downstream gene expression is a fundamental question in systems biology. Although experiments have shown that molecular degradation strongly influences downstream rhythmic responses, a general quantitative theory explaining how degradation, stochastic bursting, and upstream timing variability jointly govern rhythm transmission remains lacking. Here we develop a general analytical framework based on a martingale-based orthogonal decomposition, applicable to arbitrarily complex upstream dynamics, including memory effects. We derive exact autocorrelation and power-spectrum transmission laws, establish an oscillation-efficiency contraction principle, and identify a critical degradation rate that provides a necessary and sufficient condition for stochastic rhythm transmission. An explicit rhythm-transmission relation reveals that increasing burst frequency and modulation depth promotes rhythm transmission, whereas greater variability in upstream cycle duration suppresses it. In particular, increasing burst size leaves oscillation efficiency unchanged. The predicted degradation threshold correctly separates all ten pulsing and nonpulsing p53 target proteins reported in previous experiments. These results provide a theoretical foundation for understanding how cells selectively preserve or integrate rhythmic regulatory signals.

papers.title: Optimal climate policy in incomplete electricity markets
papers.summary: Incomplete long-term contracting in electricity markets can expose investors and consumers to inefficient levels of risk. This paper investigates how incompleteness impacts the optimal choice of climate policy. We develop a game-theoretic model of optimal policy-making in anticipation of how electricity market agents react to a given policy when gas prices and demand are uncertain and contracting is incomplete. In illustrative experiments, we observe that renewable subsidies and carbon prices induce an insurance co-benefit when markets are incomplete. This is because, relative to a complete market benchmark, incompleteness shifts investment from renewables toward gas and exposes consumers to uninsured risk from inter-annual volatility in electricity prices. By incentivizing investment in renewables, subsidies and carbon prices indirectly counteract these distortions. Consequently, incompleteness increases the optimal subsidy and carbon price levels in our experiments. Renewable subsidies exhibit a stronger insurance effect than carbon pricing, as the latter leads to more investment in gas with carbon capture and storage and more volatile electricity prices. While carbon pricing is more economically efficient than subsidies in complete markets, incompleteness shrinks its efficiency advantage and even leads to cases where subsidies are more economically efficient.

papers.title: Flash Word : ESL Listening Support with Subtitle Skimming
papers.summary: Listening to English audio with English subtitles is thought to be effective for ESL students to improve listening comprehension skills. However, for those who learn English as a second language it can be hard to finish English subtitles. Also they are unlikely to focus on listening while being busy reading subtitles. We propose Flash Word, a subtitling system which generates and presents shortened intralingual subtitles for English audio by detecting keywords from the script. Flash Word extracts keywords from scripts using an existing algorithm, and shows them one at a time like a flashcard. The system calculates when the keywords are being pronounced and aligns them correctly. Flash Word aims to enable ESL students to focus better on listening by minimising the cost of reading subtitles.

papers.title: What Paid Triangles Identify about Reserve Uncertainty: Information Boundaries in Loss Reserving
papers.summary: Paid triangles identify some components of reserve uncertainty while others enter through modelling assumptions. We distinguish population identification, recovery by free accident-year-level and two-stage second-moment fits, and precision at practical triangle sizes. In a compound frequency--severity hierarchy, the population law identifies the row dispersion governing non-diversifying reserve variance. With one free level per accident year, its profile likelihood attains its supremum only at homogeneity: the levels absorb realised row heterogeneity on every triangle, in amounts and in counts. Anchoring reopens this channel, but supplies only one observation per accident year. On a $10 \times 10$ triangle the anchored estimate remains uncertain by a factor of several. Within-row allocation dispersion survives conditioning on row totals and hence survives free levels. In the predictive experiments, the treatment of mean-structure estimation error separated the procedures by several times more than the choice among plausible variance laws. A law of the correct form improved coverage only when its dispersion came from a prior instead of the free-level fit. On an outcome-free Schedule~P panel, no amount-only procedure approaches nominal coverage. Strongly one-sided misses reveal a displacement of realised reserves relative to the fitted predictive centres that changing the amount-only variance law cannot repair.
papers.comment: 69 pages (main text 32 pages, supplementary material pp. 33-69), 1 figure, 27 tables. R code: https://github.com/robin-vo/hgr

papers.title: Evaluating Structural and SAT Attack Resilience in Cryptographic Dynamic Logic Locking via Keystream Capping
papers.summary: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. While logic locking counters this threat by embedding key-dependent logic, conventional static key-gates remain vulnerable to both oracle-guided SAT attacks and structural removal attacks due to their time-invariant netlist signatures. Dynamic schemes such as STREAMLOCK mitigate oracle attacks by continuously masking signals with cryptographic keystream, achieving near 50\% Hamming distance output corruption under incorrect keys with low hardware overhead. However, confining key-gates to primary outputs leaves internal combinational cones vulnerable to single-tap structural bypasses. This work extends dynamic logic locking by distributing key-gates within internal paths prioritized via fault-propagation analysis. The original and internally-hardened architectures are evaluated against structural removal attacks and a bounded, unrolling-based SAT-style attack across three ISCAS'85 benchmarks. Distributing masking internally raises the uninformed attacker's brute-force search space from 6 candidate node subsets to over $10^{45}$ for the largest benchmark. Crucially, empirical analysis reveals that topological relocation alone does not prevent algebraic key extraction when wide circuits expose numerous keystream bits per clock cycle. To eliminate this leak, a keystream-bit reuse cap is introduced to restrict per-cycle exposure independent of circuit width. Under this constraint, SAT-solver tractability encounters an immediate computational cliff, transitioning sharply from rapid under-constrained solving to timeout thresholds without disclosing the secret key. Integrating fault-aware internal placement with keystream reuse capping delivers joint resilience against structural bypasses and bounded SAT attacks.

papers.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
papers.summary: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.

papers.title: LanG 2.0: Energy-Efficient Agentic AI for Semi-Automated Security Operations at Scale
papers.summary: Security operations centers (SOCs) need to turn terabytes of alerts, logs and flows into trusted, affordable decisions to unveil hidden threats. We present LanG 2.0, an agentic system that detects threats, correlates evidence and writes rules, investigating whether small local models can replace frontier models affordably and safely when structural safeguards, not model accuracy, provide the guarantees. It incorporates entity-anchored correlation, human approval of rule changes and a tamper-evident ledger. Tests span eight flow datasets from five networks, real XDR alerts and multistage campaigns. Against its predecessor, campaign correlation precision rises from 18.75% to 51.81%, and rule acceptance from at most 60.00% to 98.33%. Against Claude Opus 5.5, scoring flows against each network's normal traffic detects attacks on unseen networks at 73.42% F1 without false positives, versus 58.10% with 49.00% false positives, for at least 650 times less energy. Finetuned models statistically match it on alert classification and rule writing for 5.6 to 59 times less energy. The work demonstrates LanG's practical scalability, processing 3.33 million records in 6.4 minutes, over 30 million hourly, and its safeguards resisted prompt injection, label poisoning and ledger tampering, so small local models can carry most SOC detection affordably and safely.

papers.title: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening
papers.summary: Direct-to-biology (D2B) screening enables rapid testing of newly synthesized molecules without purification. However, uncertain concentrations in crude mixtures and limited purified-compound measurements complicate the use of these data in machine learning. Here we show that models tailored to the structure of D2B data can improve prediction and guide the discovery of more potent and selective compounds. Our assay-aware models predict activity from single-point screens, relative potency across targets from crude dose-response assays, and absolute potency from purified-compound measurements. For crude assays, potency ratios between targets tested from the same well can retain selectivity information despite uncertain concentrations. A joint model that shares information across stages and balances their contributions to training improved predictions over separate neural networks. The largest gain was in crude dose-response selectivity prediction, where rank correlation increased from 0.27 to 0.40. In a separate experiment, independently trained models guided the selection of 84 new compounds to improve ROS1 potency while limiting activity against the anti-target TRKB. Synthesis and testing identified compounds that extended the measured Pareto front, achieving better combinations of potency and selectivity than those in the training data. The most selective new compound achieved a ROS1 IC50 of 14.7 nM and 233-fold selectivity over TRKB. By comparison, the most selective training compound had a ROS1 IC50 of 20.3 nM and 79-fold selectivity. ATLAS provides the experimental setting for this approach, supporting synthesis and screening of 1,000-10,000 model-selected compounds in two- to three-week cycles. Together, these results show how assay-aware learning can use the full D2B assay sequence to guide multi-objective molecular optimization.
papers.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery (AI4DD)

papers.title: Approximate Bayesian Fusion
papers.summary: Distributed inference plays an important role in modern computational statistics and machine learning. In the frequentist setting, methods can often aggregate results by simply averaging estimators computed on data subsets. However, distributed Bayesian inference is more challenging, as it requires reconstructing the full posterior by combining subposterior distributions computed on different machines. Bayesian Fusion performs distributed Bayesian inference exactly, but at a sizeable computational cost. We propose a method that uses numerical approximations to reduce the cost of the most computationally expensive steps of Bayesian Fusion, and expands its domain of applicability. We bound the numerical error as a function of the step size of the approximation. Under regularity conditions, our approach can approximate the target posterior distribution to an arbitrary degree of accuracy, and is a practical and efficient alternative for large-scale distributed Bayesian inference. In numerical experiments on a logistic regression with more than $300{,}000$ observations, our method reaches the accuracy reported for Divide-and-Conquer Bayesian Fusion about two orders of magnitude faster. On a proportional hazards model with non-Gaussian posteriors, which lacks the lower bounds that Bayesian Fusion requires, our method reproduces funnel features of the posterior that simpler methods like Consensus Monte Carlo miss.

papers.title: Deconfinement in weak electric and magnetic fields
papers.summary: We investigate the thermal deconfinement transition in weak electric and magnetic fields, describing the hadronic phase by a pion gas and the quark--gluon plasma by the MIT bag model. Besides the thermal response of each phase, we include the one-loop electromagnetic vacuum terms of quarks and charged pions, renormalized at a common scale that fixes the charge in the confined vacuum. With no fitting of the electromagnetic response, the critical temperature rises with the electric field and falls with the magnetic one. The electric curvature is of the same size as that obtained on the lattice, while the magnetic one is a few times larger. We discuss the dependence on quark mass and renormalization scale, and a large-$N_c$ organization of both curvatures, whose sum is independent of the vacuum terms and connects directly to perturbative QCD.

papers.title: Out of sync: Accommodation, evaluation, and emergence in five weeks with an agentic AI teammate
papers.summary: As agentic AI in education shifts from reactive tools toward partners that take initiative and persist over time, a central question is how learners relate to, evaluate, and benefit from artificial agency. We conducted a longitudinal experiment in an undergraduate learning analytics course, in which 17 student teams (N = 48) collaborated with a persistent LLM-based teammate across weekly sessions. The agent decided when to intervene through a trigger-based architecture, and its social role was manipulated between teams: a Cognitive Agent that challenged quick consensus or a Supportive Agent that invited quieter members to contribute. Combining chat discourse, post-session surveys, and spoken reflections, we identified distinct patterns unfolding across three timescales. Students accommodated their language to the agent's role immediately, using more social language toward the Supportive Agent from the first session. Their helpfulness evaluations were recalibrated from session to session in relation to the agent's observed behavior, rather than remaining anchored to students' pre-existing attitudes toward AI. A slower crossover emerged in perceived collaboration process and positive-affect word use in reflections: Supportive-Agent teams began below Cognitive-Agent teams and ended above them, although students rated the Supportive Agent less helpful throughout. Because these responses follow different trajectories, single-session evaluations of agentic AI may miss changes that emerge only through repeated interaction.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to British Journal of Educational Technology

papers.title: Accept Changes, Reject Attacks: Robust Memory Management for LLM Agents
papers.summary: Since large language model (LLM) agents rely on long-term memory, what they store now shapes what they do later. A memory manager decides how each input changes this memory and which records the agent acts on. It can fail in two ways: keeping a fact that has since changed (outdated memory), or storing a planted passage or injected instruction (memory poisoning). Most prior work studies them separately, yet they call for opposite write decisions, so no fixed write rule handles both. We therefore formalize memory robustness as handling both without doing worse on other inputs. Since accuracy checks only the answer, we measure robustness with evidence-conditioned accuracy (ECA), which also checks that the records the manager selects include all the evidence the answer needs, updated and free of attacks. However, existing memory systems and defenses are not more robust than an untuned manager on our test sets. We improve robustness with a simple one-shot recipe that fine-tunes the manager on episodes synthesized around a single conversation with inserted changes and attacks. On three backbones, it improves every category score on our test sets and more than doubles the untuned manager's overall ECA, though robustness remains incomplete.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Private Federated Reinforcement Learning with Post-Quantum Authentication for Vehicular Networks
papers.summary: Federated reinforcement learning supports cooperative vehicular routing without centralizing trajectory data, but model updates may reveal private information and incur communication overhead over intermittent vehicle-to-infrastructure links, particularly when post-quantum authentication is required. We study correlated private quantization, using complementary shared randomness between paired vehicles to reduce aggregation mean squared error while preserving the marginal parameter-level local differential privacy and one-bit communication cost of independent quantization. A tunable extension mixes shared and independent randomness to bound privacy leakage given paired outputs and shared-randomness side information. For this extension, Rényi differential privacy accounting establishes vector-level local differential privacy for one model upload even when pairings are revealed. Under matched vector-level privacy and identical local and global parameters, the extension yields 16.5% lower analytical aggregation mean squared error than independent quantization. We evaluate cooperative routing by coupling traffic simulation with packet-level simulation of post-quantum-authenticated vehicle-to-infrastructure communication. Compared to full-precision updates, one-bit uploads reduce authenticated uplink size by 92.4% and increase mean verified updates aggregated per round from 19.6 to 26.5. Under mobility-constrained communication at a parameter-level privacy budget of 1, correlated private quantization reduces mean travel time by 14.3% relative to independent quantization at the same budget and communication cost. At a parameter-level privacy budget of 0.3, a vehicle-origin inference attack trained on independent simulations reaches 30% accuracy with correlated private quantization and 22% with independent quantization after 100 rounds, versus 91% without privacy and 10% for random guessing.

papers.title: Closing the Applied Cybersecurity Gap in Critical Infrastructure: A Cyber-to-Physical Security Assessment Framework for Water Systems
papers.summary: The integration of information technology and operational technology in water infrastructure creates pathways through which cyber compromise may affect physical service delivery. This study revisits the Applied Cybersecurity Gap (ACG) framework by evaluating an experimental Applied Cybersecurity Gap Index (ACGI) alongside the Cyber-to-Physical Propagation Rate (CPPR), defined as the proportion of initially compromised trials that produce a specified physical-impact outcome. The expanded evaluation comprises 2,160 synthetic trials across three water-network benchmarks, including EPANET Example Network 3 (Net3), and couples declared cyber-attack progression rules with hydraulic simulations. A source-trained machine-learning model evaluated on 247 compromised Net3 trials achieved ROC-AUC 0.772, PR-AUC 0.775, and F1 0.733, compared with 0.661, 0.642, and 0.704 for a scenario-only baseline. The configuration-cluster bootstrap interval for the ROC-AUC difference was 0.038--0.183. A separate 720-run Net3 hydraulic operating-point sensitivity analysis achieved the study's exploratory baseline pressure criterion in all reruns, preserved 717 of 720 physical-impact labels, and produced ROC-AUC 0.791 with the frozen source-trained model. Additional analyses examine the sensitivity of CPPR to the physical-impact threshold and assumed control-blocking probabilities, and demonstrate that the ACGI--CPPR association is partly induced by the simulation design rather than independently validated. The findings establish a reproducible simulation-based assessment workflow, but do not constitute field calibration of cybersecurity-control effectiveness or prediction of real-world utility incidents.

papers.title: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via hierarchical testing
papers.summary: Understanding which regulatory sequence motifs a genomic deep learning model has learned, with statistical error guarantees, is essential for trusting its use in downstream tasks such as variant effect prediction. Existing approaches to identifying which units in a trained network encode human- understandable concepts fall into two groups. Exploratory methods rank and visualize units but offer no statistical guarantee that the selected units are associated with the prediction target across the population of inputs. Testing-based methods test only single units or one pre-defined set of them, and do not control the error across the many sets of units. We introduce CUTTIE (Cluster-tree Unit Top-down Testing of Independence with Error control), which clusters the units of each layer into a tree and tests the clusters top-down with conditional independence tests, localizing information about the target while controlling the family-wise error rate. Thereby, we identify clusters that carry information about the target beyond the rest of the layer. For the units in the identified clusters, conditional attribution maps then reveal what motifs they encode. In a controlled simulation, the procedure identifies the clusters whose concepts affect the target. We apply the procedure to a convolutional model predicting cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility from DNA sequence, where the concepts encoded in the identified clusters map onto known regulatory motifs.

papers.title: Measuring Personal Information Exposure in Mental Health-Related Conversations with LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for informal mental health support, yet the privacy implications of conversational interaction remain poorly understood. Prior LLM privacy research has focused largely on model-side risks such as memorization and adversarial extraction, leaving personal information inferred from ordinary conversation understudied. We introduce a profile-recovery framework that measures personal information exposure by comparing user profiles with attributes inferred from conversation alone. We generate 240 synthetic multi-turn mental health conversations from profiles sampled from a nationally representative health survey and validate them against real counseling transcripts, finding comparable overall disclosure volume. Across 21 attributes, 33-41% of each profile is recoverable, with 76.5% first-inference and 94.3% any-of-3 accuracy. 239 of 240 conversations expose at least one sensitive mental health attribute, and 45.0\% expose all six. Our findings reveal a gap between disclosure and inferability, motivating HCI approaches to make inference risks legible and support privacy-aware interaction design.

papers.title: Dynamics of spinning test particles in the innermost stable circular orbit of an approximate Kerr-like spacetime with mass quadrupole
papers.summary: We study the motion of spinning test particles in a deformed, rotating spacetime described by a metric perturbed up to second order in the mass quadrupole moment. We examine how the parameters of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) --namely the radius, energy, and angular momentum-- are modified by the particle's spin, contrasting our findings with both the spinless case and standard Kerr benchmarks. By employing effective potential techniques, we consider both co-rotating and counter-rotating configurations, corresponding to parallel and antiparallel alignments of the angular momenta. Using the Euler--Lagrange formalism and Hamiltonian dynamics within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework, we derive an explicit general ISCO equation incorporating the spin and quadrupole parameters, alongside analytical expressions for the conserved orbital quantities. Furthermore, by taking the Schwarzschild, Lense--Thirring and Kerr limits within our generalized framework, we establish new ISCO equations and compact expressions for the energy and angular momentum that extend these fundamental spacetimes to the case of spinning test particles.

papers.title: Contribution of chromosome-naïve transposon-seeded network of DNA templates to intracellular pools of protein dimers of liquid-liquid phase-separated condensate-forming proteins
papers.summary: Molecular mechanisms governing protein-protein interactions (PPI) contributing to the biogenesis of membraneless condensates remain poorly understood. Observations reported in this contribution demonstrate that liquid-liquid phase-separated (LLPS) condensate-forming proteins and their variants harboring condensate-disrupting human pathogenic mutations are significantly enriched among PPI cascade constituents of the Hybrid Assembly Pathway (HAP) of endogenous multiprotein complexes (EMC). In contrast, no structured or disordered proteins defined as condensate-negative molecules were detected among PPI cascade constituents. Cumulative evidence derived from different lines of analytical inquiries support the concept of the significant contributions of PPI cascade constituents of HAP to the biogenesis of intracellular pools of cell type-specific protein heterodimers assembled with the engagement of at least one protein monomer selected from condensate-forming protein molecules. Analytical evidence documented in this study support the concept that genome-wide chromosome-naïve networks of transposon-seeded DNA-templates nucleate the initiation of PPI cascade chain reactions with the capacity to facilitate the concurrent iterative assembly in human cells of both the membraneless biomolecular condensates and the structured multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold 3D modelling of mutation patterns and analysis of partner-bound experimental structures identified variants located at a measured protein dimerization interface. This contribution nominates numerous protein heterodimers of potential relevance to human pathophysiology for follow-up mechanistic studies of potential fundamental and translational impacts.

papers.title: Quantum amplification of improbable futures
papers.summary: Some consequential futures consist of entirely plausible steps arranged into an unlikely sequence, such as ordinary weather anomalies combining into an extreme event or local equipment failures propagating into a widespread outage. Because the sequence as a whole carries little probability, it may be rarely observed in simulation. Quantum mechanics offers a way to change those odds: ideal amplitude amplification raises the chance of drawing such futures while preserving their relative likelihoods. For a five-state process six steps ahead, 13,888 of 15,625 futures are rare, yet together they account for about one draw in 40. We built the complete circuit in IBM's Qiskit and checked every part against an exact enumeration; four simulated rounds raised the share of rare futures drawn from 2.5% to 98.0%. On IBM's Kingston quantum computer, a two-step reference circuit that marks rare futures from a precomputed list drew them in 68.4% of shots against 43.5% for its control (z = 50); at three steps (about 1,170 two-qubit gates) the predicted signal reversed sign. Because this model's probabilities are known, every result could be checked against exact values; the mechanism is intended for simulators whose probabilities are hard to calculate, such as climate, epidemic and financial models.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables, 4 supplementary tables, graphical abstract

papers.title: Two gluon fusion into a $π^0$, $η$, or $η'$ in a relatively weak magnetic field
papers.summary: In this article, we investigate gluon fusion as a mechanism for neutral meson production ($π^0$, $η$, and $η'$), in the phenomenological context of heavy-ion collisions prior to thermalization, in which a large gluon multiplicity is expected, and when an intense background magnetic field is expected to arise. For this purpose, we computed the ratios of the emission probability rates in the presence of the background magnetic field as compared to vacuum (zero-field), as a function of transverse momenta $p_T$ and energy $\sqrt{s}$, close to midrapidity. Our theoretical results suggest a catalytic effect from the presence of the background magnetic field, that may enhance the neutral pion production by several orders of magnitude at very small energies $s \lesssim 1~\text{GeV}^2$, while the effect is negligible at larger energies $s\gtrsim 10~\text{GeV}^2$. In contrast, the $η$ and $η'$ production rates are nearly insensitive to the magnetic field presence (as compared to vacuum).

papers.title: Neural Network Methods in the 2BSDE Formalism for Solving the High-Dimensional Black--Scholes Equation with Transaction Costs
papers.summary: A 2BSDE system is written down for a $(D+1)$-dimensional Black--Scholes partial differential equation (PDE) with the Leland transaction cost model which incorporates the sign of the curvature. The 2BSDE system takes input from the ``speed'' (derivative of the curvature). This system is solved using a single ResNet neural network which learns both the solution to the PDE as well as the degrees of freedom in the curvature matrix. The network is used to learn the price of derivatives such as call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets for $D=10,100$ achieving a time-averaged RMSE of less than $0.1$ in each case.

papers.title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
papers.summary: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance. We translate this uncertain evidence into conservative engineering requirements and present a multilingual pipeline for generating and narrating low-arousal sleep stories. The implemented prototype separates deterministic planning from large language model generation, represents content and delivery parameters explicitly, shapes each script through a four-phase attention taper, validates structural and lexical constraints, performs a bounded error-aware retry, and quarantines unresolved outputs. Provider-agnostic text-to-speech synthesis is followed by paragraph-aware joining, two-pass loudness normalization, and a publication gate that re-measures the saved, encoded file against fixed loudness, loudness-range, and true-peak limits. The product data model records stop position, replay, early abandonment, and completion while treating these events as ambiguous behavioral proxies rather than clinical outcomes. We contribute an evidence-to-requirement mapping, a traceable guardrail architecture with explicit acceptance thresholds, technical evaluation criteria, and a prospective protocol for testing sleep-onset effects. No clinical efficacy is claimed; the system is positioned as a relaxation and attentional-support tool whose benefit and possible reliance must be evaluated empirically.

papers.title: Temporal and spatial couplings in the dynamics of human walking and running
papers.summary: Rhythmic behaviours such as walking and running are commonly modelled as dynamical systems around a stable limit cycle. To keep such models tractable, it is usually assumed that each step depends only on the previous one, that the limit cycle is fixed, and that the sagittal and frontal planes can be studied separately. Here, we test these assumptions in seven public datasets of human gait (71 participants), including 16 people who both walked and ran. We fit linear step-to-step maps and validate them by cross-validation, holding out more data where more data exist. At first sight, gait has memory: the state two steps back lowers the prediction error by up to 29\%. Yet most of this temporal coupling vanishes once the operating point may drift slowly and measurement noise is modelled; gait remains limit-cycle-like, around an operating point that moves. Running keeps more memory than walking in the same people. Spatial coupling between the planes is present in most participants, mainly from sagittal to frontal, but weak. This supports planar models of healthy gait, while a repeatable, task-dependent coupling index may serve as a measure of gait quality. The simple models are wrong, but useful enough.

papers.title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
papers.summary: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model. By representing membrane chemical potential barriers and active pump potentials via smoothed Eulerian kernels ($Ψ_w, \mathcal{H}_w$), we formulate the passive dynamics as an $L^2$-Wasserstein ($W_2$) gradient flow coupled to non-conservative active pushing fields representing ATP-driven $3:2$ $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ exchangers. We establish global weak existence of solutions to the continuous Poisson--Nernst--Planck--IB system via a split-step Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational scheme, backed by Calderón--Zygmund bounds for non-local Poisson drift and $H^3(\mathbb{S}^1)$ interface regularity under Stokes flow. We prove the continuous Rayleighian energy balance and establish exponential $W_2$-stability of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) under a quantitative Bakry--Émery curvature threshold. Furthermore, we analyze the dual singular limits of kernel smoothing width $w \to 0$ and dimensionless Debye length $g = λ_D / L \to 0$. We establish the precise asymptotic regime connecting regularized and sharp models, prove the $Γ$-convergence of regularized energy functionals, derive distributional interface flux jump conditions, and resolve $O(λ_D)$ Debye space-charge boundary layers to confirm bulk electroneutrality.

papers.title: Hypergraph cycle enumeration for efficient inference of planted k-XOR with smooth trade-off
papers.summary: We introduce hypergraph cycle enumeration (HCE), a simple spectral framework for detecting and recovering planted signals in noisy hypergraph inference problems. We study HCE on one representative problem from this class, namely planted noisy k-XOR, also known as sparse Learning Parity with Noise (LPN). Both theoretically and empirically, HCE achieves comparable recovery behavior to Kikuchi method, matching Kikuchi hierarchy. We identify parameter regimes where HCE outperforms Kikuchi method, showing that neither algorithm is universally better. We also show a subquadratic quantum speedup for HCE by replacing one of the algorithm's steps with a quantum walk. Our classical and quantum algorithms do not refute the quartic quantum speedup of quantum Kikuchi method, which remains valid for the practically relevant regime of large size and high noise strength.

papers.title: Robot Navigation and Canine Welfare: A Pilot Study Surfacing Challenges for Cross-Species Legibility and Proxy Validity in Animal-Machine Interaction
papers.summary: Autonomous delivery robots increasingly share residential spaces with companion animals, yet navigation behavior is rarely designed with animal welfare in mind. This paper presents a pilot study evaluating a curve-out maneuver, a laterally arcing pass-by trajectory triggered at the dog's alert distance, proposed as a candidate welfare-informed navigation intervention grounded in canine social communication research and legible motion theory. Following a research through design approach, we developed and evaluated a first design iteration of the artifact in a naturalistic home environment with a companion dog. Contrary to our hypothesis, the curve-out produced a more acute stress response than the straight-line baseline. We argue that discontinuous execution limitation, the robot stopping and reorienting multiple times to approximate the arc, undermined legibility, which in itself became a stressor. The pilot surfaces the legibility of robot behavior to non-humans' eyes and proxy stimulus validity as structural challenges for AMI and repositions the design problem for future work.

papers.title: Incorporating deep neural networks into lepton-nucleus interaction modeling
papers.summary: We present a scheme to incorporate precise inclusive cross-section predictions from a deep neural network trained on electron--carbon scattering data into a Monte Carlo event generator. The inclusive prediction is decomposed into independent exclusive interaction channels using the generator's theoretical models, and the resulting events are reweighted accordingly. We apply this scheme to investigate nuclear effects in inclusive and semi-exclusive electron-scattering measurements.

papers.title: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: We present a numerical study of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for boost-invariant flows in 2+1 dimensions. The Density Frame is a formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is first order in time, requires no auxiliary fields, and has no non-hydrodynamic modes; the only parameters are the shear and bulk viscosities and the equation of state. We formulate the numerical method in terms of a discrete analog of the dissipative function, which guarantees that the discrete equations produce entropy on all length scales and leads to a remarkably robust algorithm. We test the method against the exact solution of kinetic theory in the relaxation time approximation with Gubser symmetry. In making this comparison, we clarify how the kinetic solution matches onto hydrodynamics: we organize the solution by the opacity and show how the Bjorken attractor passes onto the Gubser solution order by order in gradients. We then replace the hydrodynamic engine of the MUSIC code with the Density Frame, and compare the two for IP-Glasma initial conditions in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. The Density Frame smooths sharp gradients more rapidly. The largest differences arise in the bulk-viscous sector, where the bulk pressure in the Density Frame responds instantaneously to the flow, while in the Müller-Israel-Stewart-based MUSIC it relaxes over a finite time. With shear viscosity alone, the multiplicity, mean transverse momentum, and elliptic flow of final-state hadrons from the two codes are very similar. The Density Frame is now ready for a complete Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion data.
papers.comment: 33 pages, 9 figures. Code available at https://github.com/derek-teaney/DFHydro

papers.title: Facets of Gravity: A journey exploring spacetime from Planckian to cosmological scales
papers.summary: What does it mean to quantize gravity, and what can a quantum theory of spacetime actually predict? This thesis explores these questions through complementary non-perturbative approaches, from the geometry of quantum spacetime to the emergence of cosmological physics. Within Causal Dynamical Triangulations, we develop observables to investigate effective topology, statistical homogeneity, and curvature in strongly fluctuating geometries, where conventional differential-geometric tools are unavailable. Tests in two-dimensional models reveal distinct coarse-graining behaviours and provide new ways to probe the emergence of familiar geometric properties. We then turn to the Functional Renormalization Group and Asymptotic Safety, developing flow invariants to characterize ultraviolet-critical surfaces and introducing Flow Invariant Neural Networks as a computational method for reconstructing them. In scalar-tensor gravity, we investigate how ultraviolet consistency conditions can constrain infrared interactions, obtaining an inflationary scenario compatible with cosmological observations. Finally, we question whether the metric must be the fundamental variable of quantum gravity. We formulate a lattice statistical approach to purely affine gravity, in which the connection is fundamental and the metric, when it exists, is emergent. Monte Carlo simulations provide exploratory results in two dimensions, while a four-dimensional homogeneous and isotropic construction yields preliminary evidence for de Sitter-like geometry and allows the study of curvature correlations. Together, these investigations develop complementary tools for studying quantum spacetime, testing its possible continuum behaviour, and connecting fundamental gravitational theories with observable physics, while identifying the conceptual and computational challenges that remain.
papers.comment: 396 pages, 68 figures, 13 chapters, 7 appendices. Extended version of the doctoral thesis, including an additional part on lattice quantum affine gravity that was added after the original manuscript assessment

papers.title: The Importance of Curium-250 to the $γ$-Ray Signature of $r$-Process Remnants
papers.summary: Identifying the astrophysical sites of the heavy rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remains one of the most prominent unsolved problems in nuclear astrophysics. Emitted $γ$-rays from the decay of unstable nuclei have been identified as a potential observable marker on both prompt and delayed timescales which could provide conclusive evidence of the presence of $r$-process activity. In this work, we identify and discuss the importance of $^{250}$Cm to the $γ$-ray spectra of remnants, showing that the decay spectrum of $^{250}$Cm dominates the $γ$-ray spectra of $r$-process ejecta across a broad timescale ($\sim$ 2,000 - 20,000 years). We highlight the uncertain nature of this spectra: $^{250}$Cm may decay via $α$-decay, $β$-decay, and spontaneous fission, but the decay branchings are not experimentally known, and each decay channel produces unique spectral lines which may be observable. We examine the potential for observation of the most prominent spectral signatures, finding that for conventional neutron star merger remnants, $γ$-ray lines will be detectable in current and future detectors only in the very near galaxy ($\sim$ 1 kpc), but other sites which could produce a larger ejecta mass may have greater observable distances. Our findings highlight the potential of actinide decay chains to indicate r-process nucleosynthesis and further underscore the necessity of measuring the nuclear properties that define their characteristic spectral signatures.

papers.title: Global Testing of Gaussian Means by Combining Marginal and Conditional Evidence
papers.summary: We propose a test of the global null hypothesis of zero means in correlated multivariate Gaussian data by combining marginal and conditional evidence at each coordinate. The conditional tests are based on the distribution of each coordinate given the remaining coordinates. At each coordinate, the corresponding two-sided $p$-values are combined using the Simes method, followed by a Bonferroni correction across coordinates. Because conditioning can either strengthen or weaken evidence against the null, neither marginal nor conditional testing is uniformly preferable. The proposed procedure adapts to their relative strengths while retaining the simplicity of minimum-type global testing. We establish finite-sample control of the global Type-I error under both known covariance and covariance estimated from an independent sample. The latter setting requires a careful analysis of the dependence between studentized marginal and conditional statistics. We evaluate the power of the proposed test through simulations, compare its performance with existing global tests, and illustrate its practical utility using a TCGA carcinoma dataset.

papers.title: Basis statistics for phylogenetic tree shape: tree balance formulas beyond expectations
papers.summary: Summary statistics that measure the shapes of phylogenetic trees contributed to quantitatively understanding evolutionary processes. Among phylogenetic summary statistics, the tree balance indices have been designed to capture intuitive notions of balance or imbalance in trees. Here, we characterize the tree balance indices in terms of basis statistics, mapping the exponentially large space of rooted, binary, unlabeled trees to lower-dimensional spaces. We observe that many tree balance indices can be represented in terms of linear functions of these low-dimensional spaces, enabling us to compute exact formulas for the means, variances, and covariances of many balance indices under the Yule--Harding model. The new framework recapitulates existing formulas for the expectations of 8 indices: Sackin index, average leaf depth, total cophenetic index, $\hat{s}$-shape statistic, Colless index, corrected Colless index, quadratic Colless index, and rooted quartet index for binary trees. It produces new formulas for the expectations of 9 additional indices: equal weights Colless index, total $I$ index, total $I'$ index, Rogers $J$ index, total internal path length, total path length, average vertex depth, stairs1 index, and stairs2 index. Moreover, the framework also allows us to calculate the exact variance of all 17 indices that are represented by the bases as well as the covariance and correlation for all $\binom{17}{2} = 136$ pairs among the 17 indices.

papers.title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
papers.summary: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $φ^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, Müller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $ω$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $ωτ_π\ll 1$, where $τ_π$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $ωτ_π$, since $τ_π\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.

papers.title: GraphTFactor: A graph-based approach for proteins transcription factor prediction
papers.summary: Transcription factors (TFs) play an important role in regulating gene expression, making their identification a fundamental task in computational biology. In this work, we propose GraphTFactor, a novel end-to-end framework that models protein sequences as graphs and directly classifies transcription factors. By encoding sequences into graph structures, the proposed approach naturally handles variable-length inputs while preserving relevant relational information, without imposing length constraints. Experimental results show that GraphTFactor outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of graph-based representations for TF prediction while providing interpretable insights into the sequence regions contributing to the model's predictions. To support reproducibility and practical adoption, we release an open-source software package and an interactive web application that let users easily perform TF prediction on custom sequences.

papers.title: Global and asymptotic properties of self-gravitating nonlinear sigma models
papers.summary: We present an analytical study of the global and asymptotic properties of static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat solutions in general relativity and its \(D\)-dimensional generalization with multiple minimally coupled scalar fields described by a general nonlinear sigma model. Assuming a complete Riemannian target space and a non-negative scalar potential satisfying suitable growth conditions, we prove that solutions remain regular at every finite nonzero radius and can be extended inward to a naked singularity at the center. In particular, this excludes singularities on spherical shells at finite radius. We further show that all solutions exhibit universal asymptotic behavior near the central singularity. Finally, we demonstrate that these spacetimes can possess at most one photon sphere, which, if present, is necessarily unstable.

papers.title: Bounds on the minimum orbital period of general static spherical black holes: a sharp upper bound and a conditional lower bound
papers.summary: We investigate bounds on the minimum orbital period around four-dimensional general static spherical black holes. For all static spherically symmetric black holes with an event horizon, asymptotic flatness and non-negative energy density outside the horizon, we prove $T_{\min}\leq 6\sqrt{3}\,πM$. The bound is sharp and is saturated by the Schwarzschild solution. The lower bound requires an additional condition on the exterior matter: under the tangential pressure condition $p_τ\geq(κ/2)ρ$ with $κ>1$, imposed for all $r\geq r_{g}$, where $r_{g}$ is the largest radius at which $T(r)$ attains its global minimum, we prove $T_{\min}\geq c(κ)M$ with $c(κ)=6\sqrt{3}π(κ-1)\sqrt{κ+2}/κ^{3/2}$. In summary, both bounds apply to the same geometric class and differ only in what they demand of the matter: non-negative energy density suffices for the upper bound, while the lower bound is established under the additional tangential pressure condition.

papers.title: Expression of White and Gray Matter Autism Functional Network Connectivity Signatures in Infancy
papers.summary: Functional connectivity studies have provided valuable insights into altered brain organization in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, most functional connectivity studies focus exclusively on either gray matter (GM) regions or white matter (WM) tracts and examine specific age groups, rather than investigating their functional interactions across brain development. This limits our understanding of how GM-WM functional interactions evolve developmentally and may obscure important aspects of brain network organization in ASD. We combined integrated WM+GM functional network connectivity (FNC) with brain-wide risk scores (BRSs) to quantify ASD-associated pattern expression in ABIDE I/II and an independent infant cohort. We employed a NeuroMark framework with predefined WM and GM intrinsic connectivity networks templates, to estimate subject-level FNC. First, we identified two distinct patterns of altered WM+GM FNC in ASD: GM-related hypoconnectivity centered on the paralimbic network and WM-GM hyperconnectivity centered on the frontal network. These findings highlight the involvement of higher-order cognitive networks and the importance of WM-GM functional interactions in characterizing ASD-related connectivity alterations. Second, infants with a higher familial likelihood of autism exhibited greater mean expression of ASD-associated FNC patterns than those with a lower familial likelihood, as quantified by BRS. These group-level findings do not establish developmental persistence or predict diagnostic outcomes at the individual level.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE 24th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)

papers.title: Effects of Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld Gravity on Black Hole Accretion
papers.summary: Black holes offer a unique setting to test gravity in the strong-field regime, where deviations from General Relativity are expected to be most pronounced. We study how modified gravity changes the structure of an advection-dominated accretion flow (ADAF) around a supermassive black hole. The gravitational field governing the disc is described by a Paczyński--Wiita-like potential derived in Eddington-inspired Born--Infeld (EiBI) gravity, formulated \textit{à la} Palatini. We solve the ADAF-like equations for this potential and compare the radial profiles of the flow with those obtained for the standard Paczyński--Wiita potential. The largest difference appears in the gas density, which is several orders of magnitude higher in the EiBI case near the inner region and converges to the standard result at large radii. The specific angular momentum and temperature are lower in EiBI gravity, while the radial velocity differs mainly at large radii for both solution branches, $ s=-1$ and $+1$. The angular velocity and the disk aspect ratio $H/r$ change only slightly. These results show that EiBI gravity can modify the density structure of hot accretion flows in the strong-field regime, potentially providing observational discriminators.

papers.title: Relating approaches to interacting quantum clocks and systems
papers.summary: The problem of describing the dynamics of quantum systems relative to quantum clocks with which they interact is relevant to the physics of quantum reference frames and quantum gravity alike. There have been different approaches that derive a relational time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system relative to the clock from a time-independent Hamiltonian constraint. We show that some of these approaches, due to Smith and Ahmadi, Gemsheim and Rost, as well as the so-called Born-Oppenheimer approach, can be unified in a single framework for describing conditional quantum states. In particular, the Born-Oppenheimer approach to quantum cosmology is seen to correspond to a type of interacting Page-Wootters formalism. We discuss the issue of unitarity and linearity, or lack thereof, in the relational dynamics, and we conclude with a brief outlook to further developments.

papers.title: Umbilic Observatories
papers.summary: We study gravitational dynamics for the simplest example of an umbilic boundary in four-dimensional general relativity --- a three-dimensional de Sitter hypersurface embedded in a four-dimensional Minkowski world. Generally speaking, an umbilic surface has the property that its induced metric is proportional to its extrinsic curvature. We consider the case of both conformal boundary conditions, as well as Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed at the timelike hypersurface. For both cases, we find that there are no linearised modes whose imaginary frequency grows with angular momentum. The conformal boundary conditions allow for a dynamical boundary degree of freedom, in addition to the bulk excitations. The umbilic property linearly decouples the boundary Weyl mode from the bulk dynamics, yielding linearly stable dynamics. In contrast, the Dirichlet problem has no boundary mode. The umbilic hypersurfaces may thus constitute an improved starting point for defining gravitational dynamics in the presence of a timelike boundary. Throughout our analysis, we draw parallels to the structure of spatial infinity for asymptotically Minkowski spacetimes and a more finite realisation thereof.

papers.title: Leaking Sound Waves: Gravitational Waves From Dark Sectors Weakly Coupled to the Standard Model
papers.summary: First-order phase transitions in a dark sector can produce an observable stochastic gravitational-wave background, and many models predicting such signals in current and future experiments have been explored. For moderately strong transitions, hydrodynamical simulations suggest that sound waves generated by the expansion and collisions of true-vacuum bubbles are the dominant source of gravitational waves. It is often assumed that these sound waves propagate only within the dark-sector fluid, while the impact of the visible sector is neglected. In this paper, we investigate the effects of a weak coupling between the dark and visible fluids on the resulting gravitational-wave signal. We adopt a phenomenological hydrodynamical description of two ultra-relativistic fluids, parametrizing their interactions without specifying an underlying microscopic model. We focus on the regime in which the coupling can be neglected during the phase transition but becomes relevant during the subsequent, longer-lasting period of sound wave propagation. Within this framework, we analytically show that, even if the bubble expansion initially affects only the dark fluid, sound waves can subsequently be induced in the visible sector. Using the sound-shell model, we find that, despite the additional sound waves generated in the visible sector, the total gravitational-wave signal sourced by both fluids is generally suppressed compared to the case of a completely decoupled dark sector. This suppression becomes more pronounced for larger interaction rates and a larger ratio of relativistic degrees of freedom in the visible sector to those in the dark sector. The coupling also modifies the shape of the gravitational-wave spectrum.

papers.title: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film
papers.summary: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character's reactions to important moments. These small, detailed edits are slow and tedious to make in standard editing tools because users have to map high-level narrative goals to low-level frame-by-frame adjustments. At the same time, these fine-scale adjustments, which we call micro-edits, can be nuanced and expressive, with different choices serving different creative goals. In this work, we start by conducting a formative study with professional editors to understand the structure of micro-edits and how they are used. We then derive a mathematical formalization for this structure to develop tools that leverage AI and optimization to make exploring micro-edits simpler and more efficient for users. Finally, we validate our tools in multiple user studies and a wide range of video examples.
papers.comment: UIST 2026 Best Paper Honorable Mention. Project page: https://microedits.github.io/

papers.title: When Does Storage Complement Solar? Investment and Cost Recovery under Advanced Net Metering
papers.summary: We examine the joint PV and storage operational and investment decisions of a prosumer under net energy metering (NEM) and peak/off-peak tariffs. Legacy NEM compensates net exports at the retail rate over a netting period, typically under time-invariant pricing. To better reflect system costs, tariff features are being reconsidered, with many U.S. states adopting time-varying prices and export compensation below the retail price. We formulate the prosumer decision problem as a cost minimization problem with charge/discharge, PV investment, and storage investment decisions. We analytically derive the optimal decisions based on the tariff's membership in one of six regions that partition the tariff space. Using these solutions, we examine the relationship between PV and storage, identifying when they are complements or substitutes. Furthermore, we identify the relationship between private DER incentives and the distribution utility's (DU's) net cost of serving the prosumer.
